# OneMind OS — Recon 02: Map / Globe Frontend Overlap

# OneMind OS — Recon 02: Map / Globe Frontend Overlap
*Generated 2026-07-06 by Legacy (direct). Read-only analysis.*
## Comparison table
| Frontend | Engine | 2D/3D | Real-time bus | WS client | Plugin arch | AI/agent control | Self-host | License |
| **WorldWideView** | CesiumJS (+ Google 3D Tiles) | 3D globe | ✅ **DataBus** (typed event bus) | ✅ WsClient.ts | ✅ PluginManager + manifests | ✅ **Agent Bus** (MCP SSE) | Docker/Next.js | Elastic 2.0 |
| WorldMonitor | globe.gl + deck.gl | 2D+3D | ❌ polling only | ❌ | ⚠️ variant configs | ⚠️ agent-bus-applier | Tauri/web | AGPL v3 |
| Osiris | MapLibre GL | 2D flat | ❌ polling | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | Next.js | MIT |
| Crucix | (globe + TAK room) | 3D | ⚠️ partial | ⚠️ | ❌ | ⚠️ briefing API | web | unknown |
| constellation-overwatch | MapLibre web components | 2D | ✅ KV watcher | ✅ | ⚠️ templ components | ❌ | Go binary | Community Copyleft |
| om-unity COP | built-in (Rust-served) | 2D map | ✅ native (in-binary) | ✅ | ❌ | ORP-QL query | single binary | Apache 2.0 |
## NATS integration readiness
- **WorldWideView — BEST.** Its `DataBus` (src/core/data/DataBus.ts) is a typed pub/sub event bus, architecturally identical to NATS. `WsClient.ts` already exists for WebSocket transport. Wiring = NATS → WebSocket bridge → `dataBus.emit(subject, payload)` → plugin renders. The `PluginManager` already routes plugin snapshots into DataBus + global store. This is a near-drop-in fit.
- **constellation-overwatch / om-unity** — both have native real-time (KV watcher / in-binary) but their UIs are tightly coupled to their own backends. Hard to repurpose as a general OneMind map.
- **WorldMonitor / Osiris** — polling-based, no bus. Would need real-time layer bolted on. Not worth it.
## Best pick: **WorldWideView** — evidence
1. **DataBus = NATS in the browser.** Typed event bus, singleton, `on/emit/off`. NATS subject → DataBus event is 1:1.
1. **WsClient already built.** No need to write WebSocket handling.
1. **PluginManager + manifests.** Each NATS subject family becomes a plugin (ships, flights, fires…). Composable, no monolith. Built-in plugins already exist: earthquakes, iss, weather, geojson.
1. **Agent Bus (docs/agent-bus.md).** HTTP+SSE write path. MCP server `szski/wwv-mcp` exposes 15 tools (globe_fly_to, layer_toggle, engine_query…). Legacy can drive the globe. Nothing else has this.
1. **CesiumJS 3D** — real globe with photorealistic tiles, horizon culling, timeline scrubber.
## What to salvage from the ones we DON'T pick
- **WorldMonitor:** the 56-layer `map-layer-definitions.ts` catalog (layer styling/config), the CII country-stress scoring algorithm, the 500+ feed list. Extract as config/docs.
- **Osiris:** the MapLibre layer rendering approach for dense point clouds (CCTV, flights), and the OSINT recon UI panels. Extract as reference.
- **constellation-overwatch:** the entity_id primitive schema + KV state aggregation pattern (already bridged). Keep entity model as docs.
- **om-unity COP:** keep as-is — it's the ORP built-in operator view, useful as a fallback/debug COP at :9090. Don't delete.
- **Crucix:** the TAK ops-room boot sequence UI and briefing generation API → reference for Legacy briefing.
## Verdict
Deploy **WorldWideView** to DOKS as the OneMind global map. Build a **NATS → WebSocket bridge** that maps subjects to DataBus events. Each data domain = one WWV plugin. Wire **Agent Bus → Legacy** so Legacy can fly the globe and toggle layers. Keep om-unity COP as debug view. Extract layer catalog + CII from WorldMonitor before deleting it.

# MOBAC — Mobile Atlas Creator

> MOBAC is the tool for building offline ATAK map packages. Download tiles from OSM, satellite imagery, USGS topo — export as map packages for ATAK. Essential for DDIL deployments where live map tiles aren't available.
https://mobac.sourceforge.io/
# What is MOBAC?
Mobile Atlas Creator (MOBAC) is an open-source tool that downloads map tiles from online sources and packages them into offline atlases for mobile and GPS applications. For ATAK, MOBAC is the primary tool for creating offline map packages — download your AO (Area of Operations) imagery while connected, deploy to ATAK for disconnected field use.
# Why It Matters for OneMind / DDIL
- DDIL operations — no internet in the field means no live map tiles; MOBAC pre-loads the AO
- ATAK map packages — operators see satellite and topo imagery on ATAK without connectivity
- Multiple zoom levels — download at street, neighborhood, and regional zoom for full coverage
- Pre-mission planning — prep the map package before deploying, distribute to all ATAK devices
# Supported Map Sources
- OpenStreetMap — standard OSM, OSM cycle, OSM transport overlays
- USGS National Maps — US topo, imagery, and elevation data
- Satellite imagery — Bing, Google (via plugins), and other tile servers
- Custom tile servers — point MOBAC at any XYZ/TMS tile server
- NZ Topo, regional maps — 30+ supported sources out of the box
# ATAK Workflow
```plain text
1. Open MOBAC → select map source (satellite, OSM topo, USGS)
2. Draw bounding box over AO (Area of Operations)
3. Select zoom levels (e.g., z10–z18 for regional to street)
4. Select output format: ATAK / TAK Map Package
5. Build atlas → exports .zip map package
6. Transfer to ATAK device (sideload via USB or TAK Server)
7. Enable in ATAK: Maps → Offline Maps → import package
8. Operators now have offline imagery at all zoom levels
```
# Output Formats
- ATAK map package (.zip) — primary format for ATAK offline maps
- OsmAnd — for OsmAnd navigation apps
- Garmin KMZ — custom maps for Garmin GPS devices
- OruxMaps, TrekBuddy, OziExplorer — 30+ supported app formats

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXXLLgsgh9w

# NYC Metro POI Overlay — Full Infrastructure

> ✅ BUILT — 127,350 placemarks across 13 toggleable layer groups. Live on Zeus's Mac at ~/Desktop/OneMind-Overlays/nyc_metro_poi_overlay.kmz
---
# How to Load in ATAK
1. Transfer the KMZ file to your device (AirDrop, Google Drive, USB, or SCP to S24 via ADB)
1. Open ATAK → Menu (hamburger) → Import → Data Package
1. Select nyc_metro_poi_overlay.kmz
1. Open Overlay Manager (layers icon) — you'll see all 13 layer groups
1. Toggle any group on/off — each expands to sub-categories
1. Tap any placemark for full details (address, phone, operator, hours, all OSM tags)
Each placemark is color-coded by group: red for emergency, orange for surveillance, purple for military, blue for transportation, etc. Labels are off by default (scale 0) so the map stays clean — tap to see details.

# How to Regenerate / Customize
The build script is at /opt/data/scripts/osm_to_kmz.py on the Legacy pod. It takes about 12 minutes to run (Overpass rate limiting slows it down).
### Change the coverage area
```python
# In osm_to_kmz.py, edit the BBOX variable:
# Format: (south, west, north, east)
BBOX = (40.45, -74.30, 40.95, -73.65)  # NYC metro
# BBOX = (34.0, -118.5, 34.1, -118.1)  # LA
# BBOX = (42.3, -71.2, 42.4, -71.0)    # Boston
```
### Add new OSM categories
Edit the BATCHES list in the script to add any OSM tag. The Overpass API supports any tag the community has mapped. See https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Map_Features for the full tag list.
```python
# Example: add wind turbines and solar farms
BATCHES.append([
    ("power", "generator", "generator:source", "wind"),
    ("power", "generator", "generator:source", "solar"),
])
```
### Rebuild from the command line
```bash
# On the Legacy pod:
cd /opt/data && python3 scripts/osm_to_kmz.py

# Output: nyc_metro_poi_overlay.kmz
# Raw JSON cache: nyc_metro_osm_raw.json
```

> Built by Legacy (Mother) on August 13, 2026 · Powered by OpenStreetMap · Overpass API · OneMind OS
# Overview
Custom KMZ map overlay built from OpenStreetMap data via the Overpass API. Covers the New York City metropolitan area (5 boroughs + surrounding NJ suburbs) with 127,350 individual points of interest organized into 13 toggleable layer groups. Designed for import into ATAK as a data package — each layer group and sub-category can be toggled on/off independently in the Overlay Manager.
This is not a live data feed. It is a static snapshot of OSM's community-mapped infrastructure as of August 13, 2026. The overlay persists on the map until removed — no NATS connection required.
---
# Why OSM/Overpass Instead of Google Maps?
Google Maps is for looking at. OSM is for extracting and building with. For sovereign map overlays, OSM is the only play.
---
# How It Was Built — Step by Step
## Step 1: Query Overpass API
The Overpass API is the read-only query endpoint for OpenStreetMap. No API key required. We queried 79 OSM tag categories across the NYC metro bounding box (40.45°S, -74.30°W, 40.95°N, -73.65°E).
Queries were batched into 11 groups (8 tags per batch) to avoid Overpass rate limiting (504 Gateway Timeout / 429 Too Many Requests). Each batch saved incrementally to a JSON cache file so progress survived timeouts.
```bash
# Example Overpass query (one batch)
curl -s "https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter" \
  --data-urlencode 'data=[out:json][timeout:120];
(
  node["amenity"="police"](40.45,-74.30,40.95,-73.65);
  node["amenity"="fire_station"](40.45,-74.30,40.95,-73.65);
  node["amenity"="hospital"](40.45,-74.30,40.95,-73.65);
  node["surveillance:type"="ALPR"](40.45,-74.30,40.95,-73.65);
);
out body;'
```
## Step 2: Categorize & Normalize
Each OSM element was classified into one of 13 layer groups based on its tags. Within each group, sub-categories provide finer granularity (e.g., Surveillance → ALPR Cameras, CCTV, Gunshot Detectors).
Each placemark carries: name (from OSM name tag), coordinates (lat/lon), address (from addr:street/housenumber), phone (from phone/contact:phone), operator (from operator tag), and all original OSM tags as description metadata.
## Step 3: Generate KML
KML (Keyhole Markup Language) is the XML format that TAK/ATAK natively imports. Each POI becomes a <Placemark> with name, description, Point coordinates, Style (icon + color), and Folder hierarchy (Group → Sub-category → Placemarks).
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<kml xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2">
  <Document>
    <Folder>
      <name>Surveillance</name>
      <Folder>
        <name>ALPR Cameras</name>
        <Placemark>
          <name>FLOCK</name>
          <description>operator=Flock Safety</description>
          <Point><coordinates>-74.0,40.7,0</coordinates></Point>
        </Placemark>
      </Folder>
    </Folder>
  </Document>
</kml>
```
## Step 4: Zip to KMZ
KMZ is simply a zipped KML file. The 63.8 MB KML compressed to 6.0 MB — small enough to AirDrop, email, or push through TAK Server. Command: zip -j output.kmz doc.kml
## Step 5: Deliver to Mac
SCP'd from the Legacy pod (DOKS) to Zeus's MacBook Pro via Tailscale egress: ~/Desktop/OneMind-Overlays/nyc_metro_poi_overlay.kmz

# Key Findings
## Surveillance Layer (Benn Jordan's Point)
1,799 ALPR cameras mapped in NYC metro alone — Flock Safety, NYPD, NYC MTA, PANYNJ, Westchester County Police all operating license plate readers. 551 additional CCTV cameras, 81 ShotSpotter gunshot detectors, 79 speed cameras. This is the crowdsourced counter-surveillance layer: OSM community members map these so anyone can see where the cameras are.
Benn Jordan's content highlighted that Flock cameras — marketed as proprietary police infrastructure — are being mapped on OSM as a transparency effort. The surveillance:type=ALPR tag was created by the community specifically for this purpose.
## Military Layer
98 military installations mapped in the NYC metro: 23 checkpoints, 27 bunkers, 45 military offices, 2 naval bases, 1 border control point. These are mostly federal installations — Fort Hamilton area, naval yards, federal building security.
## Emergency Infrastructure
254 police stations (NYPD precincts), 298 fire stations (FDNY houses), 134 hospitals, 22 ambulance stations, 1,018 emergency shelters, 103 fire hydrants. Complete first-responder overlay for the metro area.

# CoT & NATS Pipeline Context
This KMZ is the static snapshot version of what could also be a live data pipeline. The original conversation explored two approaches:
- Static (this KMZ): Query once → cache → generate KML → zip to KMZ → import into ATAK → toggle on/off. Persists on map until removed. No NATS required.
- Live (future): Publish each POI as a CoT (Cursor on Target) event atom to NATS JetStream → TAK subscribes and renders overlays in real-time. Good for dynamic data (buses, trains, traffic) but ephemeral — disappears when NATS connection drops.
For static infrastructure (police stations, hospitals, cameras), KMZ is the right choice — permanent, toggleable, no dependency on the bus.
## CoT Atom Structure (for reference)
Each POI becomes one CoT event XML atom with: UID (unique), Point (lat/lon), Type (a-u-G for ground unit), IconsetPath (icon), and Details (metadata).
```xml
<event version="2.0" uid="OSM-123456" type="a-f-G-U-CV" time="2026-08-13T12:00:00Z" start="2026-08-13T12:00:00Z" stale="2027-08-13T12:00:00Z" how="h-g-i">
  <point lat="40.7128" lon="-74.0060"/>
  <detail>
    <track speed="0" course="0"/>
    <contact name="FLOCK" phone=""/>
    <remarks>operator=Flock Safety, surveillance:type=ALPR</remarks>
  </detail>
</event>
```
## NATS Subject Taxonomy (Planned)
If this becomes a live feed, POIs would flow through the OMOS subject taxonomy:
```plain text
omos.raw.geographic.poi          ← raw OSM elements
omos.cot.ground.emergency        ← police, fire, hospital, ambulance
omos.cot.ground.infrastructure    ← fuel, power, telecom, water
omos.cot.ground.transportation    ← bus, rail, ferry, parking
omos.cot.ground.commercial        ← shops, pharmacies, food
omos.cot.ground.hazard            ← industrial, pipelines, dams
→ sinks: TAK map overlay, ClickHouse Time Machine (10yr TTL)
```

# Overpass API Technical Details
## Endpoints and Mirrors
- Primary: https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter
- Fallback: https://overpass.kumi.systems/api/interpreter
- No API key required — fully free, open
## Rate Limiting and Batching
Overpass is a community-run service with shared capacity. During peak hours (US daytime), large queries return 504 Gateway Timeout or 429 Too Many Requests. The build script handles this by:
1. Batching 79 tag categories into 11 groups (~8 tags per batch)
1. Retrying each batch 3x on primary mirror, then falling back to kumi.systems mirror
1. 10-second delay between batches to be a good citizen
1. Incremental JSON save after each successful batch — progress survives timeouts
Even with batching, some batches still hit 504 on the first attempt and needed retries. The transportation batch alone returned 35K+ elements (bus stops and parking dominate).
## Query Structure
Each batch is a single Overpass QL query that unions multiple tag selectors over the bounding box:
```plain text
[out:json][timeout:120];
(
  node["amenity"="police"](40.45,-74.30,40.95,-73.65);
  node["amenity"="fire_station"](40.45,-74.30,40.95,-73.65);
  node["amenity"="hospital"](40.45,-74.30,40.95,-73.65);
  node["surveillance:type"="ALPR"](40.45,-74.30,40.95,-73.65);
);
out body;
```
The [timeout:120] gives the server 2 minutes to respond per batch. [out:json] returns structured JSON instead of raw OSM XML.

# Elevation Data — DTED, SRTM, USGS & TAK Integration

> Elevation data gives every asset on the fabric a Z-axis — terrain awareness for drones, robots, vehicles, and operators. ATAK/CivTAK uses DTED format natively. This page unifies the format spec, all public data sources, and the OneMind pipeline for getting terrain into TAK.
---
## What Is Elevation Data?
Elevation data (Digital Elevation Models / DEMs) defines the height of the Earth's surface at every point on a grid. In TAK and OneMind it enables: terrain-following drone flight paths, line-of-sight calculations, 3D map rendering, accurate CoT altitude, and realistic simulation environments.
- Two types: DTM (Digital Terrain Model) — bare ground, no buildings/trees. DSM (Digital Surface Model) — includes all objects above ground.
- Units: meters above mean sea level (MSL) or WGS84 ellipsoid (HAE). TAK CoT uses HAE.
- Formats used in OneMind: DTED (.dt0/.dt1/.dt2), GeoTIFF (.tif), HGT (SRTM)
---
## DTED — Digital Terrain Elevation Data
> DTED is the native elevation format for ATAK, CivTAK, WinTAK, and all TAK clients. Must be in DTED format to load into TAK devices.
### Format Specification
- Developed by the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) — National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA)
- Grid-based raster format — elevation value at each lat/lon cell
- File extensions: .dt0 (Level 0), .dt1 (Level 1), .dt2 (Level 2)
- Coordinate system: WGS84 geographic (EPSG:4326)
```plain text
DTED Level | Resolution  | Cell Size    | Use Case
───────────|─────────────|──────────────|──────────────────────────────
Level 0    | 900m (~30") | ~1km grid    | Global overview, coarse terrain
Level 1    | 90m  (~3") | ~100m grid   | Regional ops, general flight
Level 2    | 30m  (~1") | ~30m grid    | Tactical ops, drone navigation
Level 3    | 10m         | ~10m grid    | High-detail (restricted, DoD only)
Level 4    | 3m          | ~3m grid     | Very high-detail (classified)

```
### File Structure
- Each file covers 1° × 1° of latitude/longitude (e.g. N40W074 = 40°N, 74°W)
- Filename convention: N40W074.dt2 → lat N40, lon W074, level 2
- Directory structure: DTED/W074/N40.dt2 (longitude folder → latitude file)
- Public DoD DTED is available only at Level 0 — Levels 1+ require DoD access or SRTM substitution
### dted.org — Public DTED API
- Site: dted.org — public DTED endpoint server for CONUS (continental US)
- Provides free DTED Level 1 (90m) and Level 2 (30m) tiles via REST API
- Coverage: Continental United States — not global
- Use for: pulling CONUS tiles for ATAK field ops, preloading NYC/Stamford area for Zeus
```bash
# dted.org API — fetch a DTED tile
# Tile for NYC area (N40W074)
curl https://dted.org/api/tile/N40W074/2 -o N40W074.dt2

# Place in ATAK DTED directory on S24
adb push N40W074.dt2 /sdcard/atak/dted/2/w074/n40.dt2

```
---
## Data Sources
### 1. USGS EarthExplorer — earthexplorer.usgs.gov
> Primary U.S. government source for elevation data. Free. Requires USGS account (free registration).
- Access: earthexplorer.usgs.gov — USGS EROS (Earth Resources Observation and Science Center)
- Datasets available: SRTM 1-Arc (30m), SRTM 3-Arc (90m), NED (National Elevation Dataset), 3DEP (1m LiDAR)
- 3DEP (3D Elevation Program): USGS national LiDAR program — 1m resolution for most of CONUS as of 2026
- Download formats: GeoTIFF, ArcGrid, IMG — convert to DTED using GDAL
- Best for: Highest-resolution CONUS data (1m 3DEP LiDAR), authoritative U.S. government source
- Note: Large area downloads require bulk order via EarthExplorer or M2M API (machine-to-machine)
```bash
# Convert USGS GeoTIFF to DTED Level 2 using GDAL
gdal_translate -of DTED -co PROFILE=DTED_2 input.tif N40W074.dt2

# Batch convert a directory
for f in *.tif; do
  gdal_translate -of DTED -co PROFILE=DTED_2 $f ${f%.tif}.dt2
done

```
### 2. SRTM — Shuttle Radar Topography Mission
- Source: NASA / NGA — Space Shuttle Endeavour radar mission (February 2000)
- Coverage: 56°S to 60°N latitude — ~80% of Earth's land surface
- Resolution: SRTM1 = 1 arc-second (~30m), SRTM3 = 3 arc-seconds (~90m)
- Format: HGT files (.hgt) — convert to DTED with GDAL
- Download: earthexplorer.usgs.gov or NASA Earthdata (search 'SRTM')
- Best for: Global coverage, offline ops outside CONUS, free with no registration for basic tiles
```bash
# Convert SRTM HGT to DTED
gdal_translate -of DTED N40W074.hgt N40W074.dt2

```
### 3. Copernicus DEM (EU)
- Source: European Space Agency (ESA) — Copernicus program
- Resolution: GLO-30 (30m global) and GLO-90 (90m global)
- Coverage: Global — better than SRTM in some regions (better void filling, updated 2021)
- Download: spacedata.copernicus.eu — free, requires ESA account
- Best for: Operations outside CONUS/NATO where SRTM has voids or low quality
### 4. CivTAK Elevation Guide — civtak.org/elevation-data
- Community resource — step-by-step guide for loading elevation data into ATAK/CivTAK
- Covers: DTED directory structure on Android, file placement, verifying terrain is active in ATAK
- Key path on Android: /sdcard/atak/dted/<level>/<lon_folder>/<lat_file>.dt<level>
- Verifying in ATAK: Settings → Elevation → check 'Use Elevation Data' is enabled
---
## Source Comparison
```plain text
Source          | Resolution | Coverage    | Free | Format  | Best For
────────────────|────────────|─────────────|──────|---------|--------------------------
dted.org        | 30–90m     | CONUS only  | ✅   | DTED    | Direct ATAK load, CONUS ops
USGS EarthExplorer | 1m–30m  | CONUS best  | ✅   | GeoTIFF | Highest res US data (3DEP)
SRTM (NASA)     | 30–90m     | 80% global  | ✅   | HGT     | Global offline ops
Copernicus DEM  | 30–90m     | Global      | ✅   | GeoTIFF | EU/global, better than SRTM
DoD DTED L2+    | 30m–10m    | Global      | ❌   | DTED    | Military ops (restricted)

```
---
## OneMind DTED Pipeline
### Step 1 — Download Tiles
```bash
# Option A: dted.org (CONUS, fastest, direct DTED)
# NYC/Stamford operational area tiles
curl https://dted.org/api/tile/N40W074/2 -o N40W074.dt2  # NYC
curl https://dted.org/api/tile/N41W074/2 -o N41W074.dt2  # Stamford CT
curl https://dted.org/api/tile/N40W073/2 -o N40W073.dt2  # Long Island

# Option B: USGS EarthExplorer (manual web UI)
# 1. Go to earthexplorer.usgs.gov
# 2. Draw AoI on map
# 3. Select dataset: SRTM 1 Arc-Second Global or 3DEP 1m
# 4. Download GeoTIFF → convert with GDAL

```
### Step 2 — Convert to DTED (if needed)
```bash
# Install GDAL
apt-get install gdal-bin  # or brew install gdal

# GeoTIFF → DTED Level 2
gdal_translate -of DTED -co PROFILE=DTED_2 input.tif output.dt2

# HGT (SRTM) → DTED Level 2
gdal_translate -of DTED N40W074.hgt N40W074.dt2

# Verify output
gdalinfo N40W074.dt2

```
### Step 3 — Load onto S24 Ultra (ATAK)
```bash
# ATAK DTED directory structure on Android
# /sdcard/atak/dted/<level>/<longitude_folder>/<latitude_file>.dt<level>

# Example: DTED Level 2 for NYC (N40, W074)
adb push N40W074.dt2 /sdcard/atak/dted/2/w074/n40.dt2

# Multiple tiles via script
for f in *.dt2; do
  # Extract lat/lon from filename (e.g. N40W074.dt2)
  lat=$(echo $f | grep -oP '[NS]\d+' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
  lon=$(echo $f | grep -oP '[EW]\d+' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
  adb push $f /sdcard/atak/dted/2/${lon}/${lat}.dt2
done

# Verify in ATAK:
# Settings → Device → Elevation → 'Use Elevation Data' = ON
# 3D map mode should now show terrain relief

```
### Step 4 — Load into PostGIS/TimescaleDB (for server-side queries)
```bash
# Convert DTED to GeoTIFF first
gdal_translate -of GTiff N40W074.dt2 N40W074.tif

# Load raster into PostGIS
raster2pgsql -s 4326 -I -C -M N40W074.tif public.elevation | \
  psql -h timescaledb-ha.geo.svc.cluster.local -U postgres -d onemind

# Query elevation at a point
SELECT ST_Value(rast, ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(-74.006, 40.7128), 4326)) AS elevation_m
FROM elevation
WHERE ST_Intersects(rast, ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(-74.006, 40.7128), 4326));

```
---
## TAK Integration — What Elevation Data Enables
- 3D terrain map in ATAK/CloudTAK/WebTAK — elevation contours, hillshade, terrain relief
- Line-of-sight (LoS) calculations — can operator at point A see asset at point B?
- Drone flight path planning — terrain-following, obstacle avoidance using DTED grid
- Accurate CoT altitude — HAE (height above ellipsoid) vs. AGL (above ground level) conversion
- FLIR Black Recon integration — autonomous path generation requires terrain mesh
- Simulation fidelity — OSSIM and Unreal Engine terrain use same DTED source
- Go2 robot terrain awareness — slope analysis, no-go zones from elevation gradient
---
## Zeus Operational Area — Pre-load Tiles
> Pre-load these tiles for NYC ↔ Stamford CT operational corridor. All available free from dted.org.
```plain text
# Zeus AO — NYC/Stamford corridor DTED Level 2 tiles
Tile        | Coverage
────────────|────────────────────────────
N40W074     | NYC, Jersey City, Newark
N40W073     | Long Island, eastern NYC
N41W074     | Stamford CT, Yonkers, lower Hudson
N41W073     | Greenwich CT, New Haven area
N40W075     | western NJ (optional)

```
---
## Implementation Status
> 📋 NOT YET LOADED — Elevation data pipeline not yet set up. ATAK devices do not currently have DTED loaded. Priority: download NYC/Stamford tiles from dted.org and push to S24 Ultra via ADB.
- 📋 Download CONUS tiles from dted.org for NYC/Stamford AO
- 📋 Push to S24 Ultra via ADB pipeline
- 📋 Load into TimescaleDB-HA PostGIS raster table for server-side LoS queries
- 📋 Integrate with FLIR Black Recon flight planning (terrain mesh)
- 📋 Feed into OSSIM simulation terrain layer
---

# Vexcel — Aerial Imagery & Geospatial Data Platform

> Vexcel is the world's largest aerial imagery and geospatial data program — 45+ countries, 99.6% U.S. population coverage. Ready-to-use, oblique, ortho, 3D, AI-enhanced, multispectral. Enterprise-grade (not free). OneMind integrates into our geo stack for training data + tactical basemaps.
---
## What Vexcel Is
- World's largest unmanned aerial imagery & geospatial data program — 45+ countries
- 99.6% U.S. population coverage (urban, suburban, rural)
- Aerial photography at 3-15cm resolution — satellites x4 clearer than drones in scale
- Ground control points matched — mapping-grade accuracy, pixel-to-data consistent
- Enterprise SaaS — not free — licensing per data type/region
- Hey HQ: Vienna, Austria (EU), US ops Houston TX
---
## Products & Services
| Product | Resolution | Type | Use Case |
| Oblique | 3in / 7.5cm | 45° angle views from 4 directions | Property inspection, urban analysis, machine vision |
| Orthomosaic (Ortho) | 3-6in / 7.5-15cm | Top-down nadir+orthorectified | Property assessment, cadastral, construction |
| TrueOrtho | 3in / 7.5cm | No building lean, highest accuracy | Detailed urban analysis, 3D modeling |
| Wide Area Ortho | 6-8in / 15-20cm | Large-area ortho coverage | Regional planning, infrastructure mapping |
| Multispectral | CIR (Color Infrared) | NIR (near-infrared) | Vegetation health, impervious surfaces, land cover |
| .Disaster Imagery | Post-disaster event response | Rapid capture events | Hurricanes, wildfires, tornadoes, flooding |
| 3D Cities | 3D model data | City digital twins | 3D visualization, simulation, planning |
| Elevate | DSM + DTM (surface models) | Elevation data | DSM for 3D, DTM for terrain analysis |
| Elements | AI-detected attributes | Semantics information | Building damage, solarPotential, vegetation health |
| On Demand | Custom requests | Specific areas/events | Custom missions, specific AOI |
## Integration Capabilities
- Vexcel Viewer — web-based world viewer for their data — WMTS/WMS compatible
- Vexcel MCP — Vector Tile Feature Server (MVT) endpoint for their data
- VectorTile API — vector tile endpoints for dynamic web maps
- Arc GIS Image Services — Esri-compatible integration
- MapControl SDK — developer SDK for embedding
- WMTS — web map tile service — OGC standard
## OneMind Integration
```plain text
Data flows:
  Vexcel API → GeoStack (Martin/TileServer GL)
    ├── MVT endpoints  → tiles on-demand
    ├── WMS endpoint   → direct rendering
    ├── WFS endpoint   → feature queries
    └── Vexcel Viewer   → embed directly

TAK Integration:
  Vexcel Data + TAK Server + Packaged Mission Data
    └── Imagery packages with embedded metadata
    └── TAK clients render mission data on their base maps

ML/AI:
  Vexcel Intelligence + OneMind → custom AI model training
  Building detection, damage assessment, vegetation health
  Property attribution — automated building attributes

```
- ✅ Ready-to-use — georeferenced, processed, QA'd — no drone/hiring pilot overhead
- 📊 Enterprise SaaS — pay per data type/region — recurring imagery cost
- 📘 Not free — pricing per coverage area/data product — but saves over drone ops
- ⚙️ Integration: vector tile API, WMTS/WMS, image services, SDK, MCP server
---
## Coverage Statistics
| Metric | Value |
| Countries | 45+ (U.S., Canada, UK, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Australia, Japan, etc.) |
| U.S. Population Coverage | 99.6% (urban, suburban, rural) |
| Resolution Range | 3in (7.5cm) to 6in (15cm) |
| Flight Fleet | Dedicated fixed-wing aircraft, calibrated cameras |
| Product Types | Oblique, ortho, TrueOrtho, multispectral, 3D Cities, elevElevate, Elements, disasters, On Demand |
---
## OneMind Fit
> Vexcel = enterprise imagery layer for OneMind.

✅ Use for: Basemaps, training data (ML/AI), 3D city models, disaster response, property analysis
❌ Don't use for: real-time tactical ops (too expensive), DoD source (classified/intel), classified areas

Deployment path:
  1. Get Vexcel API key — access to WMTS/MVT endpoints
  2. Add to CloudTAK — imagery tile server

# Esri GIS — Enterprise GIS & ArcGIS Platform

> Esri is THE enterprise GIS company. Founded 1969 — the original geospatial software. ArcGIS platform covers desktop (Pro), server (Enterprise), cloud (ArcGIS Online), developer SDKs. Used by DoD, DHS, FEMA, Fortune 500. OneMind does NOT compete with Esri full-suite — wins via open, real-time, tactical intelligence.
---
## What GIS Is (Esri's definition)
- GIS = technology that connects data to a map — location data (where) + descriptive data (what)
- Purpose: map, analyze, communicate patterns, relationships, conditions
- Four use cases: choosing location, finding best route, keeping track, planning for future
---
## ArcGIS Full Stack
```plain text
Desktop: ArcGIS Pro (primary), ArcMap (legacy, deprecating)
Server: ArcGIS Enterprise (self-hosted web GIS), Portal for ArcGIS (content mgmt)
Cloud: ArcGIS Online (SaaS), ArcGIS Hub (community), StoryMaps, Dashboards
Developer SDKs: JavaScript, Native (iOS/Android), .NET, Qt, Unreal, Unity
Field Apps: Collector, Survey123, QuickCapture — mobile data collection

```
## ArcGIS Products (Key)
| Product | What It Is | OneMind Relevance |
| ArcGIS Pro | Desktop GIS — analysis, cartography | 🔄 Competitive |
| ArcGIS Enterprise | Self-hosted web GIS backend | 🔄 Competitive |
| ArcGIS Online | SaaS web GIS platform (below) | 🔄 Competitive |
| ArcGIS Hub | Community engagement portal | ⚪ External |
| ArcGIS StoryMaps | Narrative spatial storytelling | ⚪ Public communication |
| ArcGIS Dashboards | Real-time ops dashboards | 🔄 Competitive |
| ArcGIS Field Ops | Mobile collection (Collector, Survey123) | ⚪ TAK integration possible |
| 3D Tiles in Esri | 3D Tiles support since Pro 2.8 | ⚪ We use CesiumJS with 3D Tiles |
## OneMind vs Esri Comparison
| Capability | Esri ArcGIS | OneMind OS |
| Deployment | Windows Server | Kubernetes — any infra |
| Architecture | Windows-only, proprietary | Linux-native, open-source, K8s-first |
| Real-time | ArcGIS Dashboards — polling | NATS pub/sub — event-driven |
| 3D Globe | ArcGIS Pro 3D | CesiumJS — full web 3D |
| Mobile | ArcGIS Field Apps (iOS/Android) | Flutter — any platform |
| Data Format | File Geodatabase (proprietary) | Open: GeoJSON, GeoParquet, MVT, COG, 3D Tiles |
| ML/AI | ArcGIS Pro + partner models | NATS + any ML (Bedrock, vLLM) |
| Pricing | Enterprise licenses per user/product | FOSS base — no license fees |
| Suitability | Government standards, large orgs | Emerging tech, tactical, startups |

# Cesium — 3D Geospatial Globe & Visualization Platform

> Cesium is THE open platform for 3D geospatial — the world's most accurate web-based globe engine. OneMind already uses Cesium for TAK 3D view (tak3d.tail717ba0.ts.net). Google, Komatsu, NVIDIA, Unity, Unreal Engine are official partners. 15.6k stars, 46k commits, basis of CesiumJS (open source), Cesium ion (SaaS data), 3D Tiles (OGC standard), Cesium for Unity and Cesium for Unreal
## What It Is
- Open platform for 3D geospatial software development
- The globe engine: renders WGS84 Earth with terrain/imagery in any browser
- 3D Tiles: OGC community standard for streaming massive 3D datasets (buildings, point clouds, terrain)
- enant: 3D Tiles Next → glTF extensions for city-scale AEC workflows
- Community: 15.6k GitHub stars, 46k commits, Fedora Forums active, contributor program
---
## Cesium Products
```plain text
Product            | What It Is | Status in OneMind
───────────────────|────────────|───────────────────────────────────────────
CesiumJS           | Open-source JavaScript 3D globe library | ✅ USED — tak3d.tail717ba0.ts.net
Cesium ion         | SaaS platform — 3D tiling, hosting, streaming | ⚪ Optional — could use for terrain/imagery
3D Tiles           | OGC standard for streaming massive 3D | ✅ Via CesiumJS
Cesium for Unity   | Unity engine integration (XR/VTOL) | 🚧 PLANNED — Unity 7 + Unreal page
Cesium for Unreal  | Unreal Engine plugin | 🚧 PLANNED — Unity 7 + Unreal page
Cesium for Omniverse| NVIDIA Omniverse connector | ⚪ Available if needed
Sandcastle         | Live code playground + examples | ✅ For testing

```
---
## CesiumJS — The OneMind Usage
> TAK 3D View: tak-webview-cesium pod in takserver ns serves CesiumJS 3D map from TAK Server CoT data — shows drones, aircraft, ground units on 3D globe. URL: tak3d.tail717ba0.ts.net
```plain text
Architecture:
  TAK Server CoT (UDP multicast)
    └──► takserver-nats (TAK↔NATS bridge) → fabric.tak.cot
          └──► takserver Postgres (mission DB)
                └──► tak-webview-cesium pod serves the CesiumJS UI
                      └──► Browser renders 3D globe with live CoT tracks

Data flow:
  NATS cots → JSON → CesiumJS Entity API → 3D model/position on globe

```
- Currently: self-hosted CesiumJS on a K8s pod — full control, no external deps
- Imagery: local or provider (Bing/Aerial) via Cesium ion token (optional)
- Value: 3D perspective = see drone altitude, LOS obstructions, terrain effects
---
## 3D Tiles — The Streaming Standard
- OGC standard for streaming massive 3D datasets — geospatial equivalent of HLS/DASH for video
- OGC 3D Tiles 2.0 = glTF extensions for AEC (CAD-like workflows)
- Data types: city models (3D buildings), point clouds, terrain, photogrammetry
- Sources: ContextCapture, Pix4D, LIDAR surveys — any 3D Tiles source renders in Cesium
## Cesium for Unity + Cesium for Unreal
> 🚧 PLANNED — Unity 7 + Unreal Engine 5 page covers the XR/VR cross-engine combination. Cesium for Unity + Unreal are the 3D globe layers in those engines. This is how you build VR TAK/AR overlay tools.
- Cesium for Unity: full Cesium globe inside Unity projects (XR/VR/AR/mobile/desktop)
- Cesium for Unreal: full Cesium globe inside Unreal Engine 5 (high-fidelity 3D)
- Both are Apache 2.0, official Cesium products — not third-party hacks
## OneMind geospatial rendering stack
```plain text
Data layers (bottom to top):
  Base      → Cesium World Terrain / ion imagery (optional)
  Street    → OpenStreetMap via Martin tile server
  Geo-vec   → Martin (tiles: pg_featureserv, STAC API)
  Imagery   → CloudTAK tiles / WebODM orthos
  3D Mesh   → 3D Tiles from photogrammetry / LiDAR

🌐 CesiumJS (web)
   └── Renders all layers above in 3D globe view

🖥️ omos-ui (Flutter)
   └── MapLibre → 2D tactical map (primary)
   └── Cesium via WebView → secondary 3D view

🎮 Unity 7 + Unreal 5 (planned)
   └── Overlays Cesium globe in Unity/Unreal projects
   └── XR/VR/AR applications

```
## TAK Integration — Why Cesium Matters
- TAK Server 5.7: CoT data flows to TAK WebTAK UI (2D) + tak-webview-cesium (3D)
- 3D view: See droppoint altitude, terrain blocking LOS, building heights in urban operations
- CloudTAK: data packages stream to CesiumJS for 3D view of shared mission data
- VRTAK (planned): Cesium for Unity in VR headset — full 3D mission in VR
## Cesium ion — Terrain & Imagery Service
```plain text
Cesium ion provides:
  • Cesium World Terrain — quantized-mesh terrain tiles
  • Bing Maps Aerial imagery
  • Global 3D building models
  • Point cloud data sources

OneMind: ⚪ Not using ion SaaS yet — self-hosted CesiumJS works without it
  → Future: paid ion tier for global 3D buildings + terrain
  → Alternative: AWS 3D Tiles (Amazon provides NYC, SF, etc. buildings)

```
- Optional: ion s free tier covers basic usage — signup, generate token, use in CesiumJS
- Alternative: self-host terrain tiles from SRTM/ETOPO1 global elevation
## Relevant Links
- CesiumJS: github.com/CesiumGS/cesium — open source, 15.6k stars
- Cesium ion: cesium.com/ion — SaaS 3D data platform
- 3D Tiles Spec: ogc.org/standards/3DTiles
- Cesium for Unity: github.com/CesiumGS/cesium-unity
- Cesium for Unreal: github.com/CesiumGS/cesium-unreal
- Sandcastle (live playground): sandcastle.cesium.com — try examples without install
---
## Next Steps
```plain text
IMMEDIATE:
  □ tak3d view — verify CesiumJS pod healthy in takserver ns
  □ Sandcastle Copilot — try AI-assisted globe building
  □ Add Cesium ion free token → Bing imagery in tak3d

SOON:
  □ Cesium for Unity → VR/AR TAK overlay (VRTAK)
  □ Cesium for Unreal → high-fidelity training sim
  □ 3D Tiles from WebODM photogrammetry (buildings, terrain)

FUTURE:
  □ 3D Tiles 2.0 — vector data in 3D (roads, parcels in volumetric view)
  □ Custom terrain from LiDAR surveys
  □ Omniverse Cesium → digital twin of facilities

```
---
> Cesium in OneMind: already used for TAK 3D view. Cesium for Unity/Unreal connects to the planned VRTAK/XR efforts. 3D Tiles standard is the data backbone — investigate generating custom 3D Tiles from WebODM photogrammetry for future training/sim.

# SkyWatch — Satellite Imagery & Geospatial Data API

> SkyWatch is the world's leading geospatial data marketplace — 700+ sensors, 95% of commercial imaging satellites, one unified API. This is the procurement layer. Vexcel = data provider (one of hundreds). SkyWatch = marketplace connecting buyers to ALL providers. Already serves 150K+ users, 12M+ km² delivered in 12 months, 8M+ API calls.
---
## What SkyWatch Is
- Geospatial data marketplace — one catalog, one API to 700+ data providers
- One POST to order, one GET to receive — satellite/aerial/drone imagery
- Services: Identity, Archive & Tasking, Order Management, Fulfillment, Payments, Policy, Locations
- AI Data Advisor — describe your problem in plain language, get imagery recommendations
- Archive or task fresh captures — same API for both
---
## Scale
| Metric | Value |
| Sensors & data sources | 700+ |
| Commercial imaging satellites covered | 95% |
| Users on platform | 150,000+ |
| Data delivered last 12 months | 12 million km² |
| API calls handled | 8M+ in last 12 months |
| Active organizations | 7,500+ |
---
## SkyWatch Products (The 5 Pillars)
| Product | Purpose | OneMind Use |
| Explore | Search catalog, compare providers, transparent pricing, purchase | Imagery procurement |
| Hub | Procure, store, manage, share across org | Centralized procurement + licensing |
| Map | Direct integration into ArcGIS/QGIS desktop | Pull data into existing GIS |
| Build | Developer API — one POST/one GET — embed imagery | OneMind programmatic imagery |
| Connect | Sell your data to 150K+ buyers | If OneMind captures proprietary data |
---
## SkyWatch API — One POST, One GET
> Their core promise: 'ship features, not infrastructure'. Single API to 400+ (now 700+) providers.
```bash
# STEP 1: Place an order with one POST
curl -X POST https://api.skywatch.com/v1/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SKYWATCH_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "aoi": "-122.42,37.77,-122.39,37.80",
    "resolution": "0.5m",
    "source": "archive"
  }'
# → Returns order_id, status, estimated_delivery

# STEP 2: Retrieve delivered data with one GET
curl https://api.skywatch.com/v1/orders/ord_8fa2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SKYWATCH_API_KEY"
# → status: "delivered"
# → format: "COG + STAC"
# → download_url: presigned URL

```
- AOI = Area of Interest — bbox or GeoJSON polygon
- Resolution filter: 0.3m, 0.5m, 1m, 10m, etc.
- Source filter: archive (existing) or tasking (fresh capture)
- Output: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) + STAC metadata
- Delivery: presigned S3 URLs — direct download or stream
---
## Platform Services
| Service | What It Handles |
| Identity | User creation, KYC validation, role/permission management |
| Archive & Tasking | Search 700+ sensors, order existing or task fresh captures |
| Order | Schedule delivery, maintain status, notify on completion |
| Fulfillment | Ingest from providers, quality check (cloud cover %), stitch |
| Payments | E-commerce for small-parcel imagery, anti-fraud, sales tax |
| Policy | Pricing rules, permissions, territory/AOI restrictions |
| Locations | Geocoding, AOI processing, stored search areas |
## Data Types Available
- Optical: True-color, NIR, SWIR bands — from Pleiades, Planet, SkySat, WorldView, SPOT
- SAR: Radar imagery — day/night, all-weather — from Capella, ICEYE, Umbra
- Hyperspectral: 100+ bands — material identification — from Pixxel, Orbital Sidekick
- Aerial: Fixed-wing and helicopter surveys — like Vexcel data (Vexcel IS a SkyWatch provider)
- Drone: Local drone captures from partners
- Open Data: Free sources — Sentinel, Landsat — also via same API
---
## OneMind Integration
```plain text
Data flow into OneMind geo stack:

  SkyWatch API (order)
    └──► Presigned S3 URL
          └──► COG + STAC item
                ├──► STAC API pod (geo ns) → catalog discovery
                ├──► TimescaleDB → metadata → STAC items
                ├──► TiTiler → COG → tile service
                └──► Martin → vector overlay

Use cases:
  • Basemap imagery for TAK/omos-ui (via TiTiler)
  • Tasking fresh captures for AOIs (mission prep)
  • SAR over cloudy regions (day/night, all-weather)
  • Change detection (archive timestamps compare)
  • ML training datasets (ordered previews → bulk)

```
---
## Vexcel vs SkyWatch
| Aspect | Vexcel | SkyWatch |
| Role | Data provider — owns aircraft + cameras | Marketplace — aggregates 700+ providers |
| Coverage | 45+ countries (their flights) | Global (all providers) |
| Resolution | 3-6in (aerial) | 0.3m+ (satellite), 3-6in (aerial via providers) |
| Pricing | Subscript或/per-area licensing | Pay-per-use + subscription |
| OneMind role | Imagery supplier | Imagery gateway — access Vexcel + others |
| API | WMTS/MVT/Salesforce/ImageServer | REST + STAC + COG |
> SkyWatch is an aggregator — Vexcel is a provider you access THROUGH SkyWatch (or direct). OneMind gets both: SkyWatch for breadth + flexibility, Vexcel direct for their high-res aerial areas.
---
## Integration Path for OneMind
```plain text
IMMEDIATE:
  □ Sign up at skywatch.com → get API key
  □ Query NYC/Stamford AOI → see available imagery
  □ Run curl order → receive COG in minutes
  □ Add COG to TiTiler/STAC catalog

BUILD:
  □ SkyWatch → Redpanda Connect feed → on-demand imagery ingest
  □ Policy engine: auto-order imagery when AOIs marked
  □ SkyWatch MCP tool — Legacy can 'order imagery' naturally

SCALE:
  □ Budget controls + approval workflow in Hub
  □ Auto-tasking for high-priority AOIs
  □ ML pipeline: order preview → train model → bulk order for training

```
---
## Industries Served
- AEC — construction site monitoring, planning
- Energy/Oil/Gas — pipeline inspection, site monitoring
- Forestry — canopy health, land-use change
- Agriculture — crop health, field conditions
- Insurance — property risk, claims verification
- Government — public safety, urban planning
---
## Relevant Links
- Main site: https://skywatch.com
- Developer docs: https://docs.skywatch.com
- API reference: https://docs.skywatch.com/api-reference
- Explore UI: https://app.skywatch.com — search + buy
---
> SkyWatch = procurement gateway for geospatial data. Vexcel is one of 700+ providers. OneMind uses SkyWatch as the marketplace for ONE API to satellite/aerial imagery — then stores it in our own geo stack (STAC catalog, TiTiler, Martin) and delivers it via TAK mission packs to TAK clients.

# Remote Sensing & GIS Glossary — Earth Observation Terms

> Source: SkyWatch Remote Sensing & GIS Glossary. All terms from the EO/geospatial domain — essential vocabulary for working with satellite imagery, TAK, QGIS, PostGIS, and the OneMind geo stack.
---
# — A —
**Aerial Imagery***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
Imagery captured from crewed aircraft flying below satellite altitude. Typically offers very high spatial resolution over a defined area. Well suited to detailed mapping and inspection of cities, sites, and infrastructure.
**Albedo***  [Analysis & Indices]*
The fraction of incoming sunlight a surface reflects, from 0 (fully absorbing) to 1 (fully reflecting). Snow and ice have high albedo; forests and asphalt have low albedo — useful in climate, energy, and land-cover analysis.
**Analysis-Ready Data (ARD)***  [Processing & Formats]*
Satellite data already corrected, calibrated, and standardized — typically georeferenced, atmospherically corrected, and tiled — so analysts can use it immediately without heavy pre-processing.
**Area of Interest (AOI)***  [Access & Tasking]*
The specific geographic area you want imagery for, usually drawn as a polygon or bounding box. Your AOI defines what gets searched, priced, tasked, and delivered.
**Atmospheric Correction***  [Processing & Formats]*
The process of removing the effects of the atmosphere — haze, scattering, and absorption — from raw imagery, so pixel values reflect ground conditions rather than the air in between. Essential for comparing imagery over time.
---
# — B —
**Band***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
A discrete range of wavelengths a sensor records, such as red, green, blue, or near-infrared. Combining bands in different ways produces natural-color views, false-color composites, and spectral indices.
**Basemap***  [GIS Fundamentals]*
The reference layer of imagery or cartography that other geospatial data is drawn on top of. Provides geographic context — roads, terrain, or recent satellite imagery — without being the primary subject of analysis.
**Bathymetry***  [Analysis & Indices]*
The measurement of water depth and the shape of underwater terrain. Satellite-derived bathymetry uses how light penetrates and reflects through shallow water to map coastlines, reefs, and seabeds.
---
# — C —
**Change Detection***  [Analysis & Indices]*
Comparing imagery of the same location captured at different times to identify what has changed — new construction, deforestation, flooding, or encroachment. One of the highest-value workflows in Earth observation.
**Cloud Cover***  [Resolution & Quality]*
The percentage of an image obscured by clouds. High cloud cover can make optical imagery unusable, which is why analysts filter by it — and why cloud-penetrating radar (SAR) matters in persistently cloudy regions.
**Coordinate Reference System (CRS)***  [GIS Fundamentals]*
The framework that ties coordinates in your data to real positions on Earth, defining the datum, projection, and units. Two datasets must share a CRS — or be reprojected to one — before they can be accurately overlaid.
---
# — D —
**Digital Elevation Model (DEM)***  [Analysis & Indices]*
A 3D representation of terrain elevation stored as a grid of height values. Underpins orthorectification, flood modeling, line-of-sight analysis, and slope and viewshed calculations. See also: DTED, SRTM.
**Digital Surface Model (DSM)***  [Analysis & Indices]*
An elevation model that includes everything on the surface — buildings, vegetation, and structures — in addition to the bare ground. Useful for measuring heights of objects and modeling line of sight.
**Digital Terrain Model (DTM)***  [Analysis & Indices]*
An elevation model of the bare earth with surface features like buildings and trees removed. Used for hydrology, engineering, and terrain analysis where the underlying ground matters.
**Drone Imagery (UAV)***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
Imagery collected by uncrewed aerial vehicles flying at low altitude. Delivers extremely high resolution over small areas on demand — ideal for close inspection, surveying, and progress monitoring of individual sites.
---
# — E —
**Earth Observation (EO)***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
The collection of information about Earth's physical, chemical, and biological systems using remote sensing — primarily satellites, aircraft, and drones. The umbrella term for the entire field.
**Electromagnetic Spectrum***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
The full range of energy wavelengths, from radio waves to gamma rays. Remote sensing instruments record specific portions — visible light, infrared, microwave — and each reveals different things about the surface.
---
# — F —
**False-Color Composite***  [Analysis & Indices]*
An image that maps non-visible bands (such as near-infrared) to visible colors to highlight features the eye can't normally see. A common false-color view renders healthy vegetation in bright red.
**Feature Extraction***  [Analysis & Indices]*
Automatically identifying and outlining objects of interest in imagery — buildings, roads, water bodies, vehicles — to turn raw pixels into structured, mappable data.
**Footprint***  [Access & Tasking]*
The area on the ground covered by a single image or scene. Comparing an image's footprint to your AOI tells you how much of your target area a given capture actually contains.
---
# — G —
**Geographic Information System (GIS)***  [GIS Fundamentals]*
Software for storing, analyzing, visualizing, and managing spatial data. Platforms like ArcGIS and QGIS let teams combine imagery with other layers — parcels, assets, sensors — to answer location-based questions.
**Georeferencing***  [Processing & Formats]*
Assigning real-world coordinates to an image so each pixel maps to a known location on Earth. Without it, imagery can't be measured, overlaid, or compared accurately against other data.
**GeoTIFF***  [Processing & Formats]*
A widely used raster image format that embeds georeferencing information — coordinate system and position — directly in the file, so imagery opens in the right place in any GIS without a separate world file.
**Ground Control Point (GCP)***  [Processing & Formats]*
A location whose precise coordinates are known on the ground and identifiable in an image. GCPs are used to georeference and orthorectify imagery, improving positional accuracy.
**Ground Sample Distance (GSD)***  [Resolution & Quality]*
The real-world distance represented by one pixel in an image — e.g. 30cm GSD means each pixel covers a 30cm square on the ground. Smaller GSD = finer detail. Often used interchangeably with spatial resolution.
---
# — H —
**Hyperspectral Imaging***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
Imaging that captures hundreds of narrow, contiguous spectral bands, producing a detailed spectral fingerprint for every pixel. Can distinguish materials and minerals that look identical in ordinary color imagery.
---
# — I —
**Incidence Angle***  [Resolution & Quality]*
The angle at which a sensor views a target relative to straight down (nadir). Larger off-nadir angles let satellites see to the side and revisit faster, but can distort geometry and stretch ground resolution.
**Interferometry (InSAR)***  [Analysis & Indices]*
A radar technique that compares the phase of two or more SAR images to measure tiny ground movements — millimeters of subsidence, uplift, or structural shift — over time.
---
# — L —
**LiDAR***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
Light Detection and Ranging — an active sensor that fires laser pulses and times their return to build precise 3D point clouds of terrain, structures, and vegetation, even penetrating tree canopy to map the ground beneath.
---
# — M —
**Metadata***  [Processing & Formats]*
Descriptive information packaged with an image: when and where it was captured, by which sensor, at what resolution, cloud cover, sun angle. Metadata is how you find, filter, and trust imagery.
**Mosaic***  [Processing & Formats]*
A single seamless image assembled by stitching together multiple overlapping scenes. Mosaics provide continuous coverage of an area too large for one capture.
**Multispectral Imaging***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
Imaging that records a handful of broad spectral bands — typically red, green, blue, and near-infrared. Supports natural-color views plus vegetation, water, and land-cover analysis. The workhorse of optical EO.
---
# — N —
**Nadir***  [Orbits & Platforms]*
The point on the ground directly beneath a sensor. A nadir view looks straight down, giving the truest geometry and least distortion; off-nadir views look to the side.
**NDVI***  [Analysis & Indices]*
Normalized Difference Vegetation Index — a ratio of near-infrared to red reflectance that measures vegetation health and density. Values near 1 = dense healthy vegetation; low values = bare soil, water, or stress.
---
# — O —
**Optical Imagery***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
Imagery formed from reflected sunlight in the visible and infrared bands — the familiar photographic satellite view. Information-rich but depends on daylight and clear skies. Contrast with SAR.
**Orbit***  [Orbits & Platforms]*
The path a satellite follows around Earth. Earth-observation satellites usually fly in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) for detail, with the specific orbit determining coverage, revisit frequency, and lighting conditions.
**Orthorectification***  [Processing & Formats]*
Correcting an image for terrain relief, sensor tilt, and viewing geometry so every pixel sits in its true map position. Orthorectified imagery can be measured and overlaid like a map.
---
# — P —
**Panchromatic***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
A single-band image recording overall brightness across a wide visible range, usually at higher spatial resolution than color bands. Often fused with color bands via pan-sharpening.
**Pan-sharpening***  [Processing & Formats]*
Merging a high-resolution panchromatic band with lower-resolution color bands to produce a single image that is both sharp and in color — combining the best of each.
**Pixel***  [Resolution & Quality]*
The smallest element of a digital image. Each pixel represents a measured patch of ground; how much ground it covers is the image's ground sample distance (GSD).
**Point Cloud***  [Processing & Formats]*
A set of 3D points, each with a position and often color or intensity, describing the shape of surfaces and objects. Produced by LiDAR and by photogrammetry from overlapping imagery.
---
# — R —
**Radiometric Resolution***  [Resolution & Quality]*
How finely a sensor distinguishes differences in energy or brightness, expressed in bits. Higher radiometric resolution (e.g. 12-bit vs 8-bit) captures subtler tonal variation in shadows and highlights.
**Raster***  [GIS Fundamentals]*
Data stored as a grid of cells or pixels, each holding a value — the structure of all imagery and continuous surfaces like elevation. Contrast with vector data (points, lines, polygons).
**Remote Sensing***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
Gathering information about an object or area from a distance — without physical contact — typically by measuring reflected or emitted energy from satellites, aircraft, or drones. The core method behind Earth observation.
**Resampling***  [Processing & Formats]*
Recalculating pixel values when an image is reprojected, resized, or aligned to a new grid. Method chosen (nearest-neighbor, bilinear, cubic) affects sharpness and accuracy of the result.
**Revisit Time***  [Orbits & Platforms]*
How often a satellite or constellation can image the same location. Shorter revisit times = fresher data and finer change detection — daily or multiple times per day with large constellations.
---
# — S —
**Spatial Resolution***  [Resolution & Quality]*
The level of ground detail an image captures, defined by the size of the smallest distinguishable feature — closely tied to GSD. Higher spatial resolution reveals smaller objects.
**Spectral Resolution***  [Resolution & Quality]*
The number and narrowness of spectral bands a sensor records. Higher spectral resolution — as in hyperspectral imaging — lets you distinguish materials with similar appearance but different spectral signatures.
**Spectral Signature***  [Analysis & Indices]*
The characteristic pattern of how a material reflects and absorbs energy across wavelengths. Water, vegetation, soil, and minerals each have distinct signatures, allowing spectral data to identify what's on the ground.
**Sun-Synchronous Orbit (SSO)***  [Orbits & Platforms]*
A near-polar orbit timed so the satellite passes over each location at roughly the same local sun time on every revisit. Consistent lighting makes images far easier to compare across days and seasons.
**Supervised Classification***  [Analysis & Indices]*
Sorting image pixels into land-cover classes using training samples an analyst has labeled. The algorithm learns from the examples, then assigns every pixel to the most similar class.
**Swath Width***  [Orbits & Platforms]*
The width of the strip of ground a sensor images in a single pass. Wider swaths cover more area per orbit, supporting broad monitoring; narrow swaths often trade coverage for higher resolution.
**Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
An active radar sensor that emits microwave pulses and measures their echo, building imagery independent of sunlight and able to see through clouds, smoke, and darkness — invaluable for all-weather, day-or-night monitoring.
---
# — T —
**Tasking***  [Access & Tasking]*
Commissioning a satellite to capture new imagery of a specific location at a future time, rather than buying from the existing archive. Tasking gets you fresh data of exactly the area and window you need.
**Temporal Resolution***  [Resolution & Quality]*
How frequently imagery of a location is available over time — essentially the cadence of revisit. High temporal resolution is what makes monitoring and timely change detection possible.
**Thermal Infrared***  [Sensors & Data Types]*
The portion of the infrared spectrum tied to heat emitted by surfaces. Thermal imagery reveals temperature differences — useful for detecting fires, equipment activity, water stress, and urban heat islands.
**True-Color Composite***  [Analysis & Indices]*
An image combining the red, green, and blue bands to show a scene roughly as the human eye would see it from above. The most intuitive way to view optical imagery.
---
# — U —
**Unsupervised Classification***  [Analysis & Indices]*
Grouping image pixels into clusters by statistical similarity without pre-labeled training data. The analyst interprets and labels the resulting clusters afterward — useful when ground truth is scarce.
---
# — V —
**Vector***  [GIS Fundamentals]*
Spatial data represented as discrete geometry — points, lines, and polygons — with attached attributes, such as building outlines or road networks. The complement to raster data in a GIS.
---
# — W —
**Web Map Service (WMS / WMTS)***  [Access & Tasking]*
Open standards for streaming map imagery over the web as rendered tiles or images. Pull live layers straight into a GIS or web app without downloading and hosting the full dataset.
---

# ArcGIS Online — SaaS Web GIS Platform

> ArcGIS Online is Esri's SaaS product — hosted web GIS platform. FedRAMP Moderate + ISO 27001 certified. Fortune 500 trusts it. Integrates with Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Azure, Autodesk.
---
## What ArcGIS Online Is
- Hosted SaaS web GIS platform — zero infrastructure to deploy
- FedRAMP Moderate + ISO 27001 certified for US government use
- Works online + offline — maps sync when connection returns
- Thousands of resources: sample code, templates, pre-built apps, AI models
---
## Key Features
| Feature | What It Does |
| 2D/3D Maps | Interactive maps, immersive 3D scenes |
| Real-time Data | IoT/sensor feeds, live updates |
| Analysis Tools | Spatial joins, pattern detection, what-if scenarios, forecasting |
| AI-Enhanced | ML-enhanced analysis with Esri AI stack |
| Data Management | Collection, governance, enterprise scale |
| Sharing | Public/private sharing, embedded maps, StoryMaps |
| Developer Tools | ArcGIS Maps SDKs: JS, native mobile, .NET, Qt, Unreal, Unity |
| Field Apps | Collector, Survey123, QuickCapture — mobile data collection |
## OneMind vs ArcGIS Online
> OneMind does NOT compete head-on with ArcGIS Online.

ArcGIS Online = general enterprise GIS — mapping, analysis, dashboards, communications.
OneMind = dynamic tactical intelligence — real-time CoT, NATS bus, agent reasoning, physical AI coordination.

Win: same-day deployment, every platform, any machine, agent integration, open source, Linux-native.
| Capability | ArcGIS Online | OneMind OS |
| Real-time CoT | Polling dashboards | NATS pub/sub — live every |
| Voice/TAK | No native voice | LiveKit + om-presence + TAK |
| Agent AI | ArcGIS ML tools | Legacy mother — full orchestration |
| Mobile | ArcGIS Field Apps | Flutter — any platform |
| 3D Globe | Cesium via ArcGIS JS SDK | CesiumJS native — self-hosted |
| Deployment | SaaS only | K8s, edge, homelab, airgap |
| Cost | Per-user licensing | FOSS base |
---
## Relevant Links
- ArcGIS Online: esri.com/arcgis/products/arcgis-online
- ArcGIS Hub: hub.arcgis.com — community engagement portal
- StoryMaps: storymaps.arcgis.com — narrative spatial storytelling
- ArcGIS Developers: developers.arcgis.com
---
## OneMind Fit
- 🔄 Complement: ArcGIS for general use, OneMind for tactical/dynamic
- ✅ OneMind wins: real-time, Linux/K8s, agentic, open, portable
- ⚪ ArcGIS wins: general mapping, enterprise integrations, FedRAMP

# SkyWatch — Satellite Imagery & Geospatial Data Platform

> SkyWatch is a unified geospatial data marketplace — 700+ sensors, 400+ providers, satellite imagery, aerial, drone, radar. Single account, transparent pricing, no contracts. Key to OneMind's intelligence fusion layer.
---
# 🌍 What Is SkyWatch
SkyWatch is the world's leading geospatial data platform — a marketplace and toolchain that unifies satellite imagery, aerial photography, drone data, and radar from 400+ providers into a single API, GIS plugin, and procurement workflow.
Founded in 2014, headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario. Esri Gold Partner since 2022. Used by 150,000+ users, delivered 10M+ km² of imagery in the last year.
---
# 🧩 The SkyWatch Product Family
## EXPLORE — Discover & Purchase
Web-based catalog search. Find and buy imagery from a unified archive of optical, radar, and aerial data. Compare providers side-by-side with transparent pricing before purchase.
- Filter by resolution, date, cloud cover, sensor type
- Preview footprints overlaid on the map
- Archive and tasking (order fresh captures)
- URL: https://skywatch.com/explore/
## HUB — Enterprise Procurement
Multi-team imagery procurement, storage, and spend management. Centralize purchasing, licensing, and data sharing across an org.
- Controlled team access
- Payment and licensing in one place
- URL: https://skywatch.com/hub/
## MAP — Native GIS Integration
Bring SkyWatch directly into ArcGIS Online, Enterprise, and Pro. Search, task, and ingest imagery without leaving your GIS environment.
- ArcGIS Pro Add-In (free)
- Content Store for ArcGIS Online & Enterprise
- No switching between portals or vendor contracts
- URL: https://skywatch.com/map/
## BUILD — Developer API
Pay-as-you-use REST API with access to 400+ providers. No bulk commitments, no procurement cycles. Build imagery into any application.
- 400+ providers in one API
- Transparent per-km² pricing
- Tasking, archive, delivery via API
- Docs: https://api.skywatch.com/docs
## CONNECT — Data Distribution
For satellite operators and data producers. Distribute your archive and tasking capability to 150K+ buyers. SkyWatch handles commerce, licensing, and delivery.
---
# 📡 Data Coverage
## Sensor Types
- Optical — high-res multispectral, panchromatic, RGB
- SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) — all-weather, day/night, cloud-penetrating
- Aerial — sub-meter resolution, urban detail
- Drone — ultra-high-res, custom AOI captures
- Hyperspectral — vegetation, minerals, environmental
- Video — moving imagery from satellites
## Scale
- 700+ sensors and data sources
- 95% of all commercial imaging satellites covered
- 150,000+ users on the platform
- 10M+ km² delivered in the last year
---
# 🗺️ OneMind Integration
## Why SkyWatch Matters for OneMind
OneMind's geo stack (PostGIS, Tile38, QGIS, TAK) is built to ingest, store, and display geospatial intelligence. SkyWatch is the acquisition layer — the source of fresh satellite imagery that feeds into that stack for real-time and historical analysis.
## Integration Points
### 1. QGIS Server (in geo namespace)
SkyWatch MAP ArcGIS plugin covers ArcGIS workflows. For QGIS, use the BUILD API to pull imagery tiles directly into QGIS via WMS/WMTS or direct download.
```bash
# Pull imagery via SkyWatch API into QGIS
# 1. Get API key from skywatch.com/build
# 2. Use QGIS XYZ Tiles with SkyWatch tile endpoint
# 3. Or download GeoTIFF via API and load as raster layer
```
### 2. TAK Server — Map Layers
Ingest SkyWatch imagery as KML/GeoPackage overlays into TAK. Push fresh satellite captures to all TAK clients (ATAK, WebTAK, CloudTAK) as map layers.
```bash
# Export from SkyWatch → GeoTIFF → convert to MBTiles → push to TAK
gdal_translate input.tif output.mbtiles -of MBTILES
# Upload to TAK Server data package, distribute to all clients
```
### 3. NATS Intelligence Fusion
Trigger SkyWatch API calls via Legacy when a geofence event fires on the fabric. Automatically task fresh imagery over an AOI when an alert is raised.
```json
# NATS-triggered SkyWatch tasking
# Subject: fabric.intel.skywatch.task
# Payload:
{
  "aoi": {"lat": 40.7128, "lon": -74.0060, "radius_km": 10},
  "resolution": "0.5m",
  "sensor_type": "optical",
  "triggered_by": "geofence.breach"
}
```
### 4. PostGIS — Store & Query Imagery Metadata
Store SkyWatch scene footprints, metadata, and acquisition history in PostGIS. Query available coverage by AOI and date range.
```sql
-- Query available SkyWatch scenes over NYC
SELECT scene_id, provider, resolution, acquired_at, cloud_cover
FROM skywatch_scenes
WHERE ST_Intersects(footprint, ST_MakePoint(-74.006, 40.7128)::geography::geometry)
AND acquired_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
ORDER BY acquired_at DESC;
```
---
# 🏗️ Architecture Fit
> SkyWatch sits at the top of the OneMind intelligence pyramid: Physical sensors → NATS bus → ClickHouse → SkyWatch API (tasking & archive) → PostGIS (metadata) → QGIS/TAK (display)
```bash
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            ONEMIND GEO STACK                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  TAK / QGIS / CloudTAK  ← Display Layer     │
│  PostGIS + Tile38        ← Storage Layer     │
│  SkyWatch API            ← Acquisition Layer │
│  NATS fabric.intel.*     ← Trigger Layer     │
│  Legacy (AI)             ← Decision Layer    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
---
# 💲 Pricing Model
- Pay-as-you-use — no subscriptions, no minimums, no annual contracts
- Per km² pricing shown upfront before purchase
- Credit card or prepayment
- Archive imagery: cheaper than tasking
- Tasking (fresh capture): priced per collection
- Free account to explore catalog and pricing before committing
---

- Main: https://skywatch.com
- MAP (GIS plugin): https://skywatch.com/map/
- BUILD (API): https://skywatch.com/build/
- API Docs: https://api.skywatch.com/docs
- EXPLORE (catalog): https://skywatch.com/explore/
- AI Data Advisor: https://skywatch.com (homepage)

Founders-only live global SA globe. 45+ live feeds unified: maritime vessel traffic + AIS, live aircraft contacts, ports/chokepoints/congestion, earthquakes/cyclones/volcanoes/wildfires/aurora/space weather refreshed on own cadence. # DeFlock — Crowdsourced ALPR / License Plate Reader Map

# ⚡ Zeus Intelligence Notes — Surveillance Evolution
> The trajectory of surveillance is away from cameras toward invisible, distributed sensor fusion. DeFlock maps today's visible infrastructure — what's coming has no lens.
## The Sensor Evolution Chain
```plain text
LICENSE PLATES
      ↓
    VIDEO (CCTV, Flock, ANPR)
      ↓
    BLUETOOTH (device MAC scanning)
      ↓
    RF (WiFi probes, IMSI catchers, passive SDR)
      ↓
    DRONES (aerial surveillance + sensor fusion)
      ↓
    FUSION ← NEW SENSORS → NEW DATABASE
         (no single system — everything talks to everything)
```
## The Shift: No Camera — Pure RF Sensor
> The next generation of surveillance has no lens. RF sensors are smaller, cheaper, hidden, and passive. They leave no visible footprint and require no line-of-sight.
- RF sensors detect device signatures without a camera — no image, no privacy trigger, no obvious hardware
- Smaller than a smoke detector — can be embedded in street furniture, utility boxes, signage
- Completely passive — emits nothing, only listens — nearly undetectable
- No maintenance, no lens to clean, no light requirement — works day/night/fog
- Reads: WiFi probe requests, Bluetooth advertisements, IMSI (cell), tire pressure sensors (TPMS), key fobs, AirTags
## What Gets Tracked — PLATE · TIME · PLACE · ROUTE
```plain text
PLATE     → vehicle identity (ALPR)
TIME      → when you were there (timestamp)
PLACE     → where you were (GPS/cell sector)
ROUTE     → where you came from + where you went (correlated across nodes)

Together = pattern of life. Not just where you are — where you always are.
```
## Fusion: The Person Behind the Vehicle
> The vehicle is just the first node. Fusion correlates the vehicle to the person inside it using every sensor they carry on their body.
- PHONE — WiFi probe + Bluetooth MAC + IMSI + app location pings = device fingerprint tied to vehicle plate
- WATCH — Bluetooth LE advertisement (Apple Watch, Garmin, Fitbit) — unique device ID broadcast continuously
- EARBUDS — Bluetooth broadcast (AirPods, Galaxy Buds) — additional corroborating device signature
- TIRE SENSORS — TPMS (Tire Pressure Monitoring System) broadcasts a unique ID on 315/433MHz RF — passive readers already deployed at some intersections and border crossings
- Fusion: plate + phone MAC + watch BLE + TPMS ID = individual person, not just vehicle
- Cross-reference across nodes = full route reconstruction of person, not just car
## The Future: No Cameras — Just Sensors
> The end state is a world where surveillance infrastructure is invisible. No cameras. No lenses. Just a silent RF mesh that knows where everyone is, was, and will be.
- Passive RF mesh — no active emission, no visible hardware, no legal 'camera' to regulate
- Every device a person carries becomes a beacon — opt-out is physically removing the device
- New database paradigm — not 'we have footage of you' but 'we have your signature across 400 nodes'
- TPMS unique IDs mean even a rental car with a burner phone is traceable if the tires are stock
- The countermeasure is hardware removal, not covering a lens — fundamentally different threat model
## OneMind Relevance
- DeFlock today maps the visible layer — the ALPR cameras Zeus can see and document
- The OneMind fabric should model the invisible layer too — TPMS readers, BLE scanners, IMSI catchers on the map
- Fabric Feeds: fabric.intel.surveillance.alpr.* → extend to fabric.intel.surveillance.rf.*
- TAK overlay: not just cameras as CoT points — RF sensor nodes, TPMS readers, BLE mesh as separate intel layer
- Fusion engine on NATS: correlate plate + device + TPMS hits across time → pattern of life stream

Historical change timeline per address. Surface neighboring hosts + CVEs. Use: fabric perimeter self-audit, threat actor infra mapping, dark web service discovery. Results plotted on map by GeoIP — network topology becomes a physical layer.

# North Star — Platform (nstarlive.com)

North Star is a unified 5-sector OSINT platform: Camera Globe (250k+ cameras + YOLOv8 AI), Username/Identity research, Crypto Tracing (22+ chains), NetScan (port/domain/Tor recon), and Watchtower (live global SA globe). Built on Shodan, OSM, NASA, MaxMind, GeoCLIP, YOLOv8. Subscription-based, no install. Founders-only Watchtower = maritime+aviation+hazards+infra+threats on one globe — direct parallel to what we're building on the fabric. Reference platform + potential API integration point.
