# TAK CoT Feed Sources — OneMind OS

# TAK CoT Feed Sources — OneMind OS
> Unified reference for all data sources identified across osiris, worldmonitor, worldwideview, and Crucix that can be ingested and published as Cursor on Target (CoT) XML to a TAK Server.
---
## What is CoT?
**Cursor on Target (CoT)** is a lightweight XML schema used by TAK (ATAK, WinTAK, TAK Server) to share situational awareness data across a network. Every CoT message has:
- A **type** (what kind of entity/event)
- A **UID** (unique identifier)
- A **time/start/stale** window
- A **point** with lat/lon/hae (height above ellipsoid) and CE/LE error circles
- Optional **detail** block (callsign, remarks, links, sensor data)
CoT types follow a dot-notation hierarchy: `a-f-A-M-F` = air / friendly / air / military / fixed-wing. Custom types use `b-` prefix for non-track events.
---
## Tier 1 — Real-Time Track Sources (Highest TAK Value)
These produce **moving or positional tracks** — the core of SA in TAK.
---
### 1. airplanes.live
**What it is:** Community-run ADS-B aggregation network fed by thousands of volunteer receivers worldwide. Entirely unfiltered — includes aircraft that Mode-S/FAA LADD rules hide from FlightAware/FlightRadar24.
**What you get:**
- `/v2/mil` — military aircraft only (ICAO hex ranges mapped to military operators)
- `/v2/ladd` — FAA LADD-blocked aircraft (private/sensitive operators who opted out of public tracking)
- `/v2/pia` — Privacy ICAO Address aircraft (rotating hex codes used by government/law enforcement)
- `/v2/squawk/7700` — all aircraft declaring emergency right now
- `/v2/point/{lat}/{lon}/{dist}` — all aircraft within radius of a coordinate
**CoT Type:** `a-u-A` (unknown air) or `a-f-A-M-F` (air military fixed-wing) based on ICAO hex lookup
**Auth:** None — completely free, no key
**Update Rate:** ~5–10 seconds
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/flights/route.ts`
---
### 2. ADSB.lol
**What it is:** Independent ADS-B feeder network, runs parallel to airplanes.live. Used as a fallback/cross-reference. Also provides unfiltered military/LADD/PIA/emergency feeds.
**What you get:** Same feed categories as airplanes.live — mil, ladd, pia, squawk 7700, regional
**CoT Type:** `a-u-A` / `a-f-A-M-F`
**Auth:** None — free
**Update Rate:** ~5–10 seconds
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/flights/route.ts`
---
### 3. OpenSky Network
**What it is:** Academic/research ADS-B network run out of Switzerland. Full global state vector snapshot — every tracked aircraft with position, velocity, callsign, altitude. The most complete single snapshot source.
**What you get:** Full state vectors — lat, lon, altitude, velocity, heading, callsign, ICAO hex, squawk
**CoT Type:** `a-u-A` default; enrich to friendly/hostile with ICAO hex database
**Auth:** Anonymous (limited rate) or OAuth2 (`OPENSKY_CLIENT_ID` / `OPENSKY_CLIENT_SECRET`)
**Update Rate:** ~10 seconds (anonymous), ~5 seconds (authenticated)
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/flights/route.ts`, worldmonitor `server/worldmonitor/aviation/v1/`
---
### 4. aisstream.io
**What it is:** Real-time global AIS (Automatic Identification System) vessel tracking via WebSocket. AIS is the maritime equivalent of ADS-B — every commercial vessel over 300 tons is required to broadcast. aisstream.io aggregates terrestrial and satellite AIS receivers into one stream.
**What you get:**
- Position reports (lat, lon, speed, heading, COG)
- Static data (vessel name, MMSI, IMO, call sign, vessel type, destination, ETA)
- Configurable geographic bounding boxes — subscribe to chokepoints: Strait of Hormuz, Suez Canal, Strait of Malacca, Bosphorus, etc.
**CoT Type:** `a-u-S-X-M` (unknown surface maritime) or `a-f-S-X-M` (friendly surface maritime)
**Auth:** `AISSTREAM_API_KEY` (free tier available)
**Update Rate:** Real-time WebSocket stream
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/maritime/route.ts`, Crucix `apis/sources/ships.mjs`, worldmonitor `scripts/ais-relay.cjs`
---
### 5. Wingbits
**What it is:** Commercial aircraft intelligence platform. Goes beyond raw ADS-B — enriches aircraft with owner, operator, aircraft type, and maintains a curated military/government flight database. Used by worldmonitor for enriched military flight tracking.
**What you get:**
- Live military and government aircraft positions
- Owner/operator attribution per ICAO hex
- Aircraft type, registration, photo
**CoT Type:** `a-f-A-M-F` / `a-f-A-M-H` (military helicopter) with enriched callsign/remarks
**Auth:** `WINGBITS_API_KEY`
**Update Rate:** ~10–30 seconds
**Source:** worldmonitor `server/worldmonitor/military/v1/`
---
## Tier 2 — Geospatial Event Sources (Point/Area Events)
These produce **stationary events** — alerts, incidents, detections with coordinates that map to CoT event types.
---
### 6. ACLED — Armed Conflict Location & Event Data
**What it is:** The gold standard academic conflict database. Covers battles, explosions, remote violence, riots, protests, and civilian targeting events globally. Updated within 48 hours. Maintained by a dedicated research team who code every event from open sources.
**What you get:**
- Event type (battle, explosion, protest, mob violence, etc.)
- Sub-event type (armed clash, shelling, IED, etc.)
- Exact coordinates
- Actor 1 / Actor 2 (who vs. who)
- Fatality count
- Event notes (what happened in plain text)
- Country, region, locality
**CoT Type:** `b-m-p-w` (battle/warning) for kinetic; `b-m-p-i` for IED; custom hostile event types
**Auth:** `ACLED_EMAIL` + `ACLED_PASSWORD` (free academic/non-profit registration)
**Update Rate:** ~daily batch, last 7 days queryable in real-time
**Source:** Crucix `apis/sources/acled.mjs`, worldmonitor `server/_shared/acled.ts`, worldwideview `.env.example`
---
### 7. GDELT — Global Database of Events, Language and Tone
**What it is:** Monitors print, broadcast, and online news in 100+ languages in real-time, extracts events, actors, locations, and tone. Updated every 15 minutes. One of the largest open datasets in the world — effectively a real-time global event stream derived from media monitoring.
**What you get:**
- Event type (CAMEO codes — military action, protest, arrest, attack, etc.)
- Geographic coordinates (country, city, lat/lon)
- Actors involved
- Tone/sentiment score
- Source URLs
**CoT Type:** `b-m-p` (military point) for kinetic events; `b-t-f` for protest/unrest
**Auth:** None — completely free
**Update Rate:** Every 15 minutes
**Source:** Crucix `apis/sources/gdelt.mjs`, worldmonitor `server/worldmonitor/unrest/v1/`
---
### 8. UCDP — Uppsala Conflict Data Program
**What it is:** Academic conflict dataset from Uppsala University (Sweden). Georeferenced event data on organized violence — state-based conflict, non-state conflict, one-sided violence. More curated than ACLED, slower update cadence but very precise geo data.
**What you get:**
- Event coordinates
- Conflict type
- Deaths (best/low/high estimate)
- Actors
- Country/region
**CoT Type:** `b-m-p-w` (battle warning/event)
**Auth:** `UCDP_ACCESS_TOKEN` (free registration)
**Update Rate:** Weekly batch
**Source:** worldmonitor `scripts/seed-ucdp-events.mjs`
---
### 9. NASA FIRMS — Fire Information for Resource Management System
**What it is:** NASA satellite fire detection. VIIRS (Suomi NPP) and MODIS sensors detect thermal anomalies from orbit. Coverage is global, latency is ~3 hours from satellite pass. This data is used militarily to detect strikes, vehicle fires, artillery impacts, and industrial explosions as well as wildfires.
**What you get:**
- Lat/lon of thermal anomaly
- Fire Radiative Power (FRP) — intensity in MW
- Brightness temperature
- Satellite pass time
- Confidence level (low/nominal/high)
**CoT Type:** `b-m-p-s-p-i` (point of interest — fire/thermal) or custom `t-x-c-f`
**Auth:** Free NASA earthdata account for CSV feeds; `FIRMS_MAP_KEY` for API
**Update Rate:** Every ~3 hours (per satellite pass)
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/fires/route.ts`, Crucix `apis/sources/firms.mjs`, worldmonitor `scripts/seed-fire-detections.mjs`
---
### 10. USGS Earthquake Feed
**What it is:** US Geological Survey real-time earthquake catalog. Every earthquake above a threshold magnitude is published within minutes of detection. GeoJSON format with full metadata.
**What you get:**
- Lat/lon/depth of hypocenter
- Magnitude and type (Mw, ML, etc.)
- Time of event
- Place name
- USGS event page URL
**CoT Type:** `b-n-g` (natural event/ground) or `b-m-p-s-p-i` point of interest
**Auth:** None — completely free
**Update Rate:** Near real-time (minutes after detection)
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/earthquakes/route.ts`, worldwideview `src/app/api/earthquake/route.ts`, worldmonitor `scripts/seed-earthquakes.mjs`
---
### 11. Oref / Tzeva Adom — Israel Home Front Command
**What it is:** Israeli Home Front Command's official rocket/missile alert system. When a rocket is fired toward Israel, this API publishes the alert within seconds including the target zone. Also aggregates historical alert data.
**What you get:**
- Alert zone name (city/region in Hebrew and English)
- Alert type (rocket, UAV, earthquake, tsunami)
- Timestamp
- Historical alert log
**CoT Type:** `b-m-p-w-CBRN-W` (warning) or `b-f-t-r` (rocket attack)
**Auth:** None — public endpoint
**Update Rate:** Real-time (sub-second publication)
**Source:** worldmonitor `scripts/ais-relay.cjs`
---
### 12. GDACS — Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
**What it is:** UN-run disaster alert system that aggregates data from USGS, NOAA NHC, ECHO, and other sources to produce unified global disaster alerts. Covers earthquakes, tropical cyclones, floods, volcanoes, droughts.
**What you get:**
- Event type, severity score (green/orange/red)
- Coordinates and affected area polygon
- Affected population estimates
- Event timeline
**CoT Type:** `b-n-g` (natural ground event) with severity in remarks
**Auth:** None — free RSS/API
**Update Rate:** Continuous as events occur
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/weather/route.ts`, worldmonitor `scripts/seed-natural-events.mjs`
---
### 13. NGA Maritime Safety — Navigational Warnings
**What it is:** US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency publishes active NAVTEX and broadcast navigational warnings. These include military exercise zones, mined areas, restricted operations areas, hazardous debris, and diplomatic restrictions on navigation.
**What you get:**
- Warning type and text
- Geographic coordinates / area description
- Issue authority (NAVAREA)
- Active/cancelled status
**CoT Type:** `b-m-p-w` (warning point) or area polygon overlay
**Auth:** None — public US government API
**Update Rate:** As warnings are issued/cancelled
**Source:** worldmonitor `server/worldmonitor/maritime/v1/list-navigational-warnings.ts`
---
### 14. GPSJam
**What it is:** Community-aggregated GPS interference map. Collects reports from ADS-B receivers that detect GPS jamming or spoofing (abnormal position/altitude reports). Displays heat map of interference zones updated daily. Heavily used for monitoring conflict zones — the Levant, Ukraine, and Baltic regions consistently show active jamming.
**What you get:**
- Grid cells with interference probability score
- Date of detection
- Geographic coverage
**CoT Type:** `b-m-p-j` (jamming zone) — area point/polygon
**Auth:** None — free
**Update Rate:** Daily
**Source:** worldmonitor `scripts/fetch-gpsjam.mjs`
---
### 15. DeepState Map — Ukraine Frontline
**What it is:** Ukrainian open-source intelligence project that maintains the most detailed and up-to-date Ukraine frontline map. GeoJSON polygons of Russian-controlled, Ukrainian-controlled, and contested territory updated daily by analysts.
**What you get:**
- GeoJSON polygons for territorial control
- Timestamps per update
- Named features (cities, towns, strategic locations)
**CoT Type:** Shape/polygon CoT or imported as KML overlay (already KMZ-compatible)
**Auth:** None — public API
**Update Rate:** Daily
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/frontlines/route.ts`, worldwideview (referenced)
---
### 16. AlienVault OTX — Open Threat Exchange
**What it is:** Crowd-sourced threat intelligence platform with millions of indicators of compromise (IOCs). Tor exit nodes, malicious IPs, C2 servers, botnet infrastructure. While not traditionally a TAK source, IP geolocating these indicators creates a cyber-physical threat overlay.
**What you get:**
- Malicious IP addresses with country, city, lat/lon (via ip-api)
- Threat tags and malware family
- Confidence score
**CoT Type:** `b-m-p-s-p-i` (point of interest — threat) in cyber/infrastructure layer
**Auth:** Free OTX account for full feed
**Update Rate:** Continuous
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/osint/threats/route.ts`, worldmonitor `server/worldmonitor/cyber/v1/`
---
## Tier 3 — Contextual/Enrichment Sources
These don't produce CoT directly but enrich other feeds or provide context layers.
---
### 17. CelesTrak — Satellite TLEs
**What it is:** Gold standard source for Two-Line Element orbital data for every tracked satellite. Used to compute real-time satellite positions and ground tracks. Military satellites, Starlink, GPS constellation, debris.
**CoT Use:** Satellite position tracks (`a-u-S-S` — unknown space) or ground track overlays
**Auth:** None
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/satellites/route.ts`, Crucix `apis/sources/space.mjs`
---
### 18. Safecast + EPA RadNet — Radiation Monitoring
**What it is:** Safecast is a citizen science network with 150M+ radiation readings worldwide, heavily concentrated near nuclear sites (Zaporizhzhia, Chernobyl, Fukushima, Dimona, Yongbyon, Bushehr). EPA RadNet is the US government fixed-station gamma radiation network.
**CoT Use:** Sensor point (`b-m-p-s-p-loc`) with radiation reading in detail/remarks
**Auth:** None
**Source:** Crucix `apis/sources/safecast.mjs`, worldmonitor `scripts/seed-radiation-watch.mjs`
---
### 19. ReliefWeb (UN OCHA) + UNHCR
**What it is:** UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs publishes active disaster and crisis reports with country/region coordinates. UNHCR publishes refugee population flows and displacement statistics by location.
**CoT Use:** Humanitarian crisis points with population/severity context
**Auth:** ReliefWeb requires free appname registration; UNHCR is open
**Source:** Crucix `apis/sources/reliefweb.mjs`, worldmonitor `server/worldmonitor/displacement/v1/`
---
### 20. NOAA/NWS Severe Weather Alerts
**What it is:** US National Weather Service active alerts — tornadoes, hurricanes, flash floods, blizzards, extreme heat. Polygon-based zones with severity and instructions.
**CoT Use:** `b-w-A-N-a` (weather alert) or KML polygon import
**Auth:** None — completely free US government API
**Source:** osiris `src/app/api/weather/route.ts`, Crucix `apis/sources/noaa.mjs`, worldmonitor `scripts/seed-weather-alerts.mjs`

## Architecture Notes for TAK Integration
### Option A — NATS → CoT Bridge (recommended for OMOS)
Each source becomes a NATS publisher. A bridge service subscribes, converts to CoT XML, and publishes to TAK Server via TCP (port 8087) or UDP multicast.
```plain text
Source Fetcher → NATS subject (e.g. omos.feeds.aircraft.mil) → CoT Bridge → TAK Server
```
### Option B — TAK Server Data Package
For static/slow-changing data (ACLED historical, frontlines, radiation sites): wrap as KMZ/KML in a `.dp` Data Package and push to all connected clients via TAK Server's data sync.
### Option C — Network Link KML
For large datasets (Flock cameras, ACLED, FIRMS): serve a Network Link KML endpoint that TAK polls by viewport. Only fetches what's visible at current zoom.

# Redpanda Connect — OneMind Universal Feed Engine (Technical Reference)

# Redpanda Connect (Benthos) — OneMind Universal Feed Engine
## Complete Technical Reference & Dynamic Tasking Architecture
**Author:** Zeus Delacruz / Legacy (Mother)
**Date:** August 5, 2026
**Version:** 1.0
**Purpose:** Definitive technical reference for Redpanda Connect as the OneMind feed standard
---
## 1. What Is Redpanda Connect?
Redpanda Connect (formerly Benthos) is a **declarative stream processor** — a single compiled Go binary that moves data between systems with transforms in the middle.
**Key facts:**
- **Single binary:** ~50MB, no runtime dependencies, no JVM, no Python, no Node
- **YAML-only config:** No code required for 90% of pipelines
- **200+ native components:** Inputs, processors, outputs — all compiled in, ready to use
- **Streams mode:** One binary runs N independent pipelines simultaneously
- **REST API:** Add/remove/update pipelines at runtime without restart
- **Docker image:** `redpandadata/connect:latest` (updated daily, multi-arch)
### What "Native" Means
When we say a component is **native**, we mean:
> It is part of the compiled binary. You write its name in YAML and it works.
> There is NOTHING to install, download, or configure beyond the YAML itself.
> No pip install. No npm. No plugins. No Go modules. No compilation.
> The binary ships with every component already inside it.
This is fundamentally different from Python/Node ecosystems where every capability requires installing packages. Redpanda Connect's approach: **everything is already there.**
---
## 2. Native Components We Use
### INPUTS (Sources — how data enters the pipeline)
| Component | Protocol | Our Use Cases | Polling/Streaming |
| `http_client` | HTTP/HTTPS REST | MTA, USGS, NOAA, ACLED, OpenSky, GDELT, FIRMS, cameras | Polling (configurable timer) |
| `websocket` | WebSocket | AIS maritime (aisstream.io), live news streams | Streaming (persistent connection) |
| `mqtt` | MQTT 3.1.1/5.0 | Meshtastic mesh radio, IoT sensors, Home Assistant | Streaming (subscribe to topics) |
| `socket` | Raw TCP/UDP | APRS-IS ham radio firehose | Streaming (persistent connection) |
| `http_server` | HTTP webhook receiver | Any service that can POST to us | Push (listens for incoming) |
| `generate` | Internal timer | Heartbeats, scheduled synthetic events | Polling (cron-like) |
| `nats_jetstream` | NATS JetStream | Cross-pipeline chaining, replay | Streaming (durable consumer) |
| `nats_kv` | NATS Key-Value | Watch for entity changes | Streaming (watch) |
### PROCESSORS (Transforms — what happens to data in transit)
| Component | What It Does | Our Use Cases |
| `protobuf` | Decode/encode Protocol Buffers binary ↔ JSON | MTA GTFS-RT train positions |
| `mapping` | Transform fields using Bloblang DSL | Normalize any source to common schema |
| `xml` | Parse/create XML documents | CoT event generation, RSS feeds, NOAA alerts |
| `json_schema` | Validate against JSON Schema | Ensure data quality before hitting bus |
| `dedupe` | Content-hash deduplication | Same event from multiple sources |
| `rate_limit` | Throttle throughput | Respect API rate limits (OpenSky: 1 req/10s) |
| `branch` | Conditional processing paths | Military vs civilian aircraft handling |
| `switch` | If/else routing | Route by source type or priority |
| `cache` | Read/write mid-pipeline caches | Delta filtering (has position changed?) |
| `http` | Make HTTP calls mid-pipeline | Enrich with external lookups (owner DB, etc.) |
| `log` | Debug logging | Development and troubleshooting |
| `javascript` | Run JS code inline | Complex transforms that exceed Bloblang |
| `jq` | JQ expressions | JSON filtering for complex nested structures |
| `command` | Run external binary | Shell-out for edge cases |
### OUTPUTS (Destinations — where processed data goes)
| Component | Protocol | Our Use Cases |
| `nats_jetstream` | NATS JetStream | **PRIMARY** — all feeds → JetStream streams |
| `nats` | NATS core | Lightweight fire-and-forget publish |
| `nats_kv` | NATS Key-Value | Update entity store, pattern cache |
| `broker` | Fan-out to multiple | Same message → JetStream + KV + metrics |
| `switch` | Conditional routing | Route military aircraft to special stream |
| `http_client` | HTTP POST | Webhook notifications, external APIs |
| `drop` | /dev/null | Intentionally discard (filtered events) |
### CACHES (Shared state between processors)
| Component | Backing Store | Our Use Cases |
| `memory` | In-process RAM | Delta filtering (last position per entity) |
| `nats_kv` | NATS KV bucket | Shared entity state across pipelines |
| `redis` | Redis server | If we need persistence beyond NATS KV |
### RATE LIMITS (Throttling)
| Component | How It Works | Our Use Cases |
| `local` | Token bucket per pipeline | Respect OpenSky 1req/10s, MTA 1req/30s |
---
## 3. Pipeline Anatomy
Every pipeline follows this structure:
```yaml
# metadata
label: "feed-name"

input:
  # WHERE data comes from
  http_client:
    url: "https://api.example.com/data"
    verb: GET
    rate_limit: "my_limit"

pipeline:
  processors:
    # WHAT happens to the data (in order)
    - protobuf:
        operator: to_json
        message: "transit_realtime.FeedMessage"
        import_paths: ["/proto/"]
    - mapping: |
        root.uid = this.vehicle.trip.trip_id
        root.lat = this.vehicle.position.latitude
        root.lon = this.vehicle.position.longitude
    - dedupe:
        cache: delta_cache
        key: "${! this.uid + this.lat + this.lon}"

output:
  # WHERE data goes
  nats_jetstream:
    urls: ["nats://nats:4222"]
    subject: "intel.raw.transit"

cache_resources:
  - label: delta_cache
    memory:
      default_ttl: "120s"

rate_limit_resources:
  - label: my_limit
    local:
      count: 1
      interval: "30s"
```
---
## 4. Streams Mode — One Binary, Many Pipelines
In **streams mode**, Redpanda Connect runs multiple independent pipelines from a directory of YAML files:
```bash
rpk-connect run --streams /config/pipelines/*.yaml
```
Each YAML file is an independent pipeline. They share nothing except:
- Cache resources (if configured globally)
- Rate limit resources (if configured globally)
- The NATS connection (efficient multiplexing)
**Adding a new feed = dropping a new YAML file in the directory.**
---
## 5. The REST API — Dynamic Pipeline Management
When running in streams mode with the API enabled:
```yaml
# Main config enables API
http:
  enabled: true
  address: "0.0.0.0:4195"
```
### Available Endpoints
| Method | Path | What It Does |
| GET | `/streams` | List all running pipelines |
| GET | `/streams/{id}` | Get config of specific pipeline |
| POST | `/streams/{id}` | **Create** a new pipeline (hot, no restart) |
| PUT | `/streams/{id}` | **Update** an existing pipeline |
| DELETE | `/streams/{id}` | **Stop and remove** a pipeline |
| GET | `/ready` | Health check |
| GET | `/metrics` | Prometheus metrics |
---
## 6. Dynamic Tasking — AI Creates Collection Pipelines
This is the killer feature. Legacy AI can create and destroy collection pipelines **on demand** via the REST API, triggered by TAK commands.
### The Flow

### What Makes This Powerful
1. **No deploy cycle** — Legacy doesn't need kubectl. It POSTs YAML to a REST endpoint.
2. **No orphaned processes** — DELETE the stream and collection stops cleanly.
3. **Resource bounded** — rate limits prevent runaway API calls.
4. **Auditable** — GET /streams shows all active taskings.
5. **Operator-triggered** — Zeus commands from a map. No terminal needed.
6. **AI-autonomous** — Legacy can create collection tasks WITHOUT Zeus (based on detected patterns).
7. **Composable** — tasking pipelines use the same YAML as permanent feeds.
### Legacy's Tasking Interface (Python)
```python
import httpx

CONNECT_API = "http://redpanda-connect.omos.svc.cluster.local:4195"

async def create_tasking(tasking_id: str, pipeline_yaml: str, ttl_hours: int = 72):
    """Create a dynamic collection pipeline triggered by TAK command."""
    # Create the pipeline
    resp = await httpx.AsyncClient().post(
        f"{CONNECT_API}/streams/{tasking_id}",
        content=pipeline_yaml,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/yaml"}
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200

    # Schedule TTL expiry
    await schedule_deletion(tasking_id, hours=ttl_hours)

async def delete_tasking(tasking_id: str):
    """Stop a collection pipeline."""
    resp = await httpx.AsyncClient().delete(
        f"{CONNECT_API}/streams/{tasking_id}"
    )
    return resp.status_code == 200

async def list_active_taskings():
    """Get all running pipelines (permanent + dynamic)."""
    resp = await httpx.AsyncClient().get(f"{CONNECT_API}/streams")
    return resp.json()
```
---
## 7. The Protobuf Story (MTA GTFS-RT)
MTA delivers train positions as Protocol Buffers binary. Here's exactly how Redpanda Connect handles it:
### What you need:
1. The `.proto` file (Google's GTFS-RT spec: `gtfs-realtime.proto`)
2. Mount it in the container at `/proto/gtfs-realtime.proto`
3. Reference it in the pipeline YAML
### The proto file (standard, from Google):
```protobuf
// gtfs-realtime.proto — standard Google Transit spec
syntax = "proto2";
package transit_realtime;

message FeedMessage {
  required FeedHeader header = 1;
  repeated FeedEntity entity = 2;
}

message FeedEntity {
  required string id = 1;
  optional TripUpdate trip_update = 3;
  optional VehiclePosition vehicle = 4;
  optional Alert alert = 5;
}

message VehiclePosition {
  optional TripDescriptor trip = 1;
  optional Position position = 2;
  optional string stop_id = 7;
}

message Position {
  required float latitude = 1;
  required float longitude = 2;
  optional float bearing = 3;
  optional float speed = 5;
}

message TripDescriptor {
  optional string trip_id = 1;
  optional string route_id = 5;
}
// ... (full spec at github.com/google/transit)
```
### Pipeline YAML:
```yaml
pipeline:
  processors:
    - protobuf:
        operator: to_json
        message: "transit_realtime.FeedMessage"
        import_paths: ["/proto/"]
```
**That's it.** Protobuf binary in → JSON out. The `mapping` processor then extracts fields from the JSON structure. No `pip install protobuf`. No `gtfs-realtime-bindings`. No compiled descriptors. Just the raw `.proto` file.
---
## 8. CoT XML Generation in Bloblang
The final transform before publishing to `tak.cot.inject` converts our normalized data to CoT XML:
```yaml
- mapping: |
    let ts = now().format_timestamp("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z")
    let stale = now().ts_add_duration("120s").format_timestamp("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z")

    root = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes" ?>
    <event version="2.0" type="%s" uid="%s" how="m-g" time="%s" start="%s" stale="%s">
    <point lat="%f" lon="%f" hae="0" ce="50" le="50"/>
    <detail>
    <contact callsign="%s"/>
    <track speed="%f" course="%f"/>
    <remarks>%s</remarks>
    <marti><dest mission="%s"/></marti>
    </detail></event>""".format(
      this.cot_type,
      this.uid,
      $ts, $ts, $stale,
      this.lat, this.lon,
      this.callsign,
      this.speed, this.course,
      this.remarks,
      this.mission
    )
```

## 9. Deployment Architecture
### Kubernetes Manifests
```yaml
# redpanda-connect-deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redpanda-connect
  namespace: omos
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: redpanda-connect
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: omos-intel
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: redpanda-connect
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: redpanda-connect
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: connect
          image: redpandadata/connect:latest
          args:
            - "run"
            - "--streams"
            - "/config/pipelines/*.yaml"
          ports:
            - containerPort: 4195
              name: api
          env:
            - name: NATS_URL
              value: "nats://nats.nats.svc.cluster.local:4222"
            - name: NATS_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: omos-nats-creds
                  key: user
            - name: NATS_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: omos-nats-creds
                  key: password
          volumeMounts:
            - name: pipelines
              mountPath: /config/pipelines
            - name: proto
              mountPath: /proto
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 4195
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 30
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 4195
            initialDelaySeconds: 3
            periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
        - name: pipelines
          configMap:
            name: redpanda-connect-pipelines
        - name: proto
          configMap:
            name: redpanda-connect-proto
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  na
```

## 11. Error Handling & Dead Letter Queue
```yaml
output:
  broker:
    pattern: fan_out
    outputs:
      # Primary: send to NATS
      - nats_jetstream:
          urls: ["nats://nats:4222"]
          subject: "tak.cot.inject"
      # Fallback: failed messages go to DLQ
      - fallback:
          - nats_jetstream:
              urls: ["nats://nats:4222"]
              subject: "intel.dlq.${! meta("pipeline_id")}"
```
Failed events don't vanish — they go to a dead letter queue stream that Legacy can inspect and reprocess.
---
## 12. Security
### NATS Authentication
```yaml
output:
  nats_jetstream:
    urls: ["nats://nats:4222"]
    auth:
      user: "${NATS_USER}"
      password: "${NATS_PASSWORD}"
    tls:
      enabled: true
      skip_cert_verify: true  # Internal cluster TLS
```
### API Keys for Sources
```yaml
input:
  http_client:
    url: "https://api.adsb.exchange/v2/..."
    headers:
      api-auth: "${ADSB_KEY}"  # Resolved from env var
```
All secrets come from k8s Secrets → env vars. No keys in YAML.
---
## 13. Comparison: Python Feed Pod vs Redpanda Connect
| Aspect | Python Feed Pod | Redpanda Connect Pipeline |
| **Language** | Python 3.12 | YAML (Bloblang for transforms) |
| **Dependencies** | pip install at boot (slow, fragile) | Zero (compiled into binary) |
| **Startup time** | 15-30s (pip install) | <1s |
| **Memory per feed** | ~50MB (Python runtime) | ~3-5MB (goroutine) |
| **Adding a feed** | Write Python + ConfigMap + Deployment | Write YAML file |
| **Error handling** | Manual try/except | Built-in retry, DLQ, backoff |
| **Rate limiting** | Manual sleep/counter | Declarative `rate_limit` |
| **Deduplication** | Manual dict tracking | Declarative `dedupe` + cache |
| **Health checks** | Custom probe | Built-in `/ready` endpoint |
| **Metrics** | Manual logging | Built-in Prometheus |
| **Hot reload** | kubectl rollout restart | POST/PUT to REST API |
| **Delta filtering** | 20+ lines haversine code | Cache + dedupe processor |
| **Protobuf** | pip install protobuf + bindings | Native processor + .proto file |
| **Container image** | python:3.12-alpine (50MB+) | redpandadata/connect (30MB) |
| **Deploy footprint** | 1 Deployment + 1 ConfigMap per feed | 1 Deployment total + YAML per feed |

# OneMind Feed Architecture: Before & After (Redpanda Connect)

# OneMind Feed Architecture: Before & After
## The Universal Intelligence Pipeline with Redpanda Connect
**Author:** Zeus Delacruz / Legacy (Mother)
**Date:** August 5, 2026
**Purpose:** Student reference — how we unified 100+ intel sources into a single sovereign pipeline
**Status:** IMPLEMENTATION READY
---
## What Is Redpanda Connect?
Redpanda Connect (formerly Benthos) is a **single Go binary** (~50MB) that moves data between any source and any destination with transforms in the middle. It's configured entirely in YAML — no code required for 90% of use cases.
**When we say "native" we mean:** These components are **compiled into the binary**. There is nothing to install, no plugins to download, no dependencies to manage. You write a YAML file referencing `nats_jetstream` or `http_client` or `protobuf` and it just works. The binary ships with 200+ inputs, 60+ processors, and 80+ outputs already inside it. You deploy one container image and configure everything through YAML pipeline files.
Think of it like this:
- Python feed pods = you write code for every feed (100 lines minimum)
- Redpanda Connect = you write a YAML config (20-40 lines) and the binary handles everything

## What "Native" Means — Built In, Ready to Use
When we say a component is **native** to Redpanda Connect, we mean:
> It is compiled into the binary. You reference it in YAML and it works immediately.
> No pip install. No npm. No plugins. No downloads. No dependencies.
> One container image has everything.
### Native Inputs (Sources — how data gets IN)
| Component | What It Does | Our Use Case |
| `http_client` | Polls any HTTP/HTTPS endpoint on a timer | MTA, USGS, NOAA, ACLED, OpenSky, GDELT, FIRMS, EONET, cameras |
| `websocket` | Connects to WebSocket streams | AIS maritime (aisstream.io), real-time feeds |
| `mqtt` | Subscribes to MQTT topics | Meshtastic mesh radio nodes |
| `socket` | Raw TCP/UDP connections | APRS-IS ham radio firehose |
| `http_server` | Receives webhooks / push data | Anything that can POST to us |
| `generate` | Creates messages on a schedule | Heartbeats, synthetic test data |
| `nats_jetstream` | Reads from NATS streams | Cross-pipeline chaining |
**These are not adapters or wrappers. They are first-class, production-grade implementations built by Redpanda's engineering team and maintained as part of the core project.**
### Native Processors (Transforms — what happens to the data)
| Component | What It Does | Our Use Case |
| `mapping` | Transform any field using Bloblang DSL | Normalize all feeds to common schema |
| `protobuf` | Decode/encode Protocol Buffers | MTA GTFS-RT train positions |
| `xml` | Parse XML documents | CoT events, RSS feeds, NOAA alerts |
| `json_schema` | Validate against JSON Schema | Ensure data quality before hitting bus |
| `dedupe` | Remove duplicate messages (content hash) | Same event from multiple sources |
| `rate_limit` | Throttle message throughput | Respect API rate limits |
| `branch` | Conditional processing paths | Route military vs civilian aircraft differently |
| `switch` | If/else routing | Different handling per source type |
| `cache` | Read/write to caches mid-pipeline | Entity lookup, seen-before checks |
| `http` | Make HTTP calls mid-pipeline | Enrich with external lookups |
| `log` | Log messages for debugging | Development and troubleshooting |
| `filter` | Drop messages that don't match | Only pass events inside geofence |
### Native Outputs (Destinations — where data goes)
| Component | What It Does | Our Use Case |
| `nats_jetstream` | Publish to NATS JetStream | **Primary output** — all feeds → NATS |
| `nats` | Publish to NATS core | Lightweight fire-and-forget |
| `nats_kv` | Write to NATS Key-Value store | Update entity database |
| `broker` | Fan out to multiple outputs | Same message → JetStream + KV + logs |
| `switch` | Route to different outputs conditionally | Military aircraft → special stream |
| `http_client` | POST to HTTP endpoints | Webhook notifications |
---
## What a Pipeline Looks Like (Real Example)
### feed-mta (trains) — Before (Python, 159 lines)
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import asyncio, logging, math, os, ssl, time, urllib.request, nats
from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta
from google.transit import gtfs_realtime_pb2

# 159 lines of:
# - NATS connection setup
# - Protobuf parsing
# - Delta filtering logic
# - CoT XML string building
# - Haversine distance calculation
# - Main polling loop with error handling
# - Stale time calculation
# ...
```
Required: Python image, pip install protobuf + nats-py + gtfs-realtime-bindings, ConfigMap, Deployment YAML.
### feed-mta (trains) — After (Redpanda Connect, ~45 lines YAML)
```yaml
input:
  broker:
    inputs:
      - http_client:
          url: "https://api-endpoint.mta.info/Dataservice/mtagtfsfeeds/lirr%2Fgtfs-lirr"
          verb: GET
          rate_limit: "mta_poll"
          headers:
            Accept: "application/x-protobuf"
      - http_client:
          url: "https://api-endpoint.mta.info/Dataservice/mtagtfsfeeds/mnr%2Fgtfs-mnr"
          verb: GET
          rate_limit: "mta_poll"
          headers:
            Accept: "application/x-protobuf"

rate_limit_resources:
  - label: mta_poll
    local:
      count: 1
      interval: "30s"

pipeline:
  processors:
    - protobuf:
        operator: from_string
        message: transit_realtime.FeedMessage
        import_paths: ["/config/proto/"]

    - unarchive:
        format: json_array

    - mapping: |
        # Extract vehicle positions, skip non-position entities
        root = if this.vehicle.position.latitude == 0 { deleted() }
        root.uid = "MTA-%s-%s".format(this.vehicle.trip.route_id, this.vehicle.trip.trip_id)
        root.callsign = "%s-%s".format(this.vehicle.trip.route_id, this.vehicle.trip.trip_id)
        root.lat = this.vehicle.position.latitude
        root.lon = this.vehicle.position.longitude
        root.speed = this.vehicle.position.speed.or(0)
        root.course = this.vehicle.position.bearing.or(0)
        root.source = "mta-gtfs-rt"
        root.cot_type = "a-n-G-E-V-C-R"
        root.mission = "Land"

    - dedupe:
        cache: mta_delta
        key: "${! this.uid}"
        drop_on_err: true

cache_resources:
  - label: mta_delta
    memory:
      default_ttl: "90s"

output:
  nats_jetstream:
    urls: ["nats://nats.nats.svc.cluster.local:4222"]
    subject: "tak.cot.inject"
```
**That's it.** No Python. No Docker build. No pip install. No error handling boilerplate. No connection management. Redpanda Connect handles retries, backpressure, graceful shutdown, health checks, and metrics automatically.
---
## Why This Was Built for Exactly Our Use Case
Redpanda Connect was originally created by **Ashley Jeffs** as "Benthos" — a stream processor specifically designed to move data between disparate systems with transforms in between. Redpanda (the Kafka alternative company) acquired it and rebranded it as "Redpanda Connect."
**Its design philosophy matches ours perfectly:**
| Their Design Principle | Our Need |
| "Connect anything to anything" | 50+ data sources → NATS → TAK |
| "YAML over code" | Operators (students) configure feeds without writing code |
| "Single binary, zero dependencies" | One k8s pod replaces 12 |
| "Built-in observability" | Know which feeds are healthy/stale without custom monitoring |
| "Exactly-once delivery" | Don't duplicate CoT events on the TAK map |
| "Stream processing, not batch" | Real-time positions, not 5-minute-old data |
| "Native NATS JetStream support" | Direct output to our bus — no adapter needed |
---
## The Migration — How We Get There
### Step 1: Deploy Redpanda Connect (Day 1)
```bash
# Single pod deployment in omos namespace
kubectl apply -f platform/omos/redpanda-connect.yaml
```
- Mount pipeline YAML files as ConfigMap
- Mount protobuf schemas for GTFS-RT
- Mount API keys from existing omos-feed-secrets
### Step 2: Port Existing Feeds (Week 1)
Convert each Python feed pod to a YAML pipeline:
- feed-mta → `mta-trains.yaml`
- feed-hazards → `usgs.yaml` + `noaa.yaml`
- feed-satellites → `satellites.yaml`
- feed-intel-* → `acled.yaml`, `firms.yaml`, `gdelt.yaml`, etc.
### Step 3: Add New Feeds (Week 2-4)
Mine omos-intel platform code for API endpoints and write new YAML pipelines:
- AIS maritime (ShadowBroker's ais-relay WebSocket)
- GDELT news events (Crucix endpoint)
- Meshtastic (ShadowBroker MQTT)
- Police scanners (ShadowBroker)
- 30+ more from the source catalog
### Step 4: Kill Old Infrastructure
- Scale all feed-* deployments to 0
- Delete the omos-intel droplet
- One Redpanda Connect pod runs everything

## For Students: The Key Concepts
### 1. The Pipeline Pattern
Every intelligence feed follows the same pattern:
```plain text
SOURCE → NORMALIZE → VALIDATE → ENRICH → ROUTE → DESTINATION
```
In Redpanda Connect: `input → pipeline.processors → output`
### 2. The Universal Bus (NATS)
All feeds publish to one bus. Consumers subscribe to what they need:
- TAK Server subscribes → gets CoT markers on the map
- ClickHouse subscribes → stores 10 years of history
- AI (Legacy) subscribes → correlates and reasons in real-time
- Future: drones, robots, AR glasses — just subscribe
### 3. Separation of Concerns
- **Collection** = Redpanda Connect (pull data from the world)
- **Transport** = NATS JetStream (move data reliably between systems)
- **Storage** = ClickHouse (remember everything for pattern detection)
- **Visualization** = TAK Server (put it on a map for humans)
- **Reasoning** = Legacy AI (find patterns, generate products, close the loop)
### 4. Configuration over Code
Adding a new intelligence source should be a **configuration change**, not a software development project. Redpanda Connect makes this possible — operators define feeds in YAML, the platform handles everything else.
### 5. Sovereignty
Every component runs on our metal, in our cluster, on our bus. No data leaves the fabric. No SaaS dependency. No vendor lock-in. We own the pipeline end to end.

## The Bidirectional Intel-Ops Loop (The Full Vision)
This pipeline doesn't just **show** data — it **acts** on data:
```plain text
Zeus drops marker in ATAK:
  "COLLECT — pattern of life — this warehouse — 72hr"
          │
          ▼
TAK → NATS (tak.cot.out) → Legacy AI sees the command
          │
          ▼
Legacy creates new Redpanda Connect pipeline dynamically:
  "Monitor ADS-B within 5km of this point"
  "Monitor social media mentioning this address"
  "Pull property records for this location"
          │
          ▼
Redpanda Connect collects → NATS → ClickHouse stores it
          │
          ▼
Legacy correlates: "Same Cessna circling at 0200, 3 nights in a row"
          │
          ▼
Legacy generates CoT product → NATS → sink-tak → TAK Server
          │
          ▼
Zeus sees the intel product on his ATAK:
  "PATTERN DETECTED: N12345 (XYZ LLC) — recurring aerial surveillance"
          │
          ▼
Zeus drops new marker: "EXPAND COLLECTION — XYZ LLC properties"
          │
          ▼
Loop continues autonomously...
```
**This is what no platform on the market offers: a sovereign, bidirectional intelligence fusion loop where the operator commands the system from a map and AI closes the loop.**
---
## Architecture Decision Record
| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| Collection engine | Redpanda Connect | YAML-only, native NATS, single binary, 200+ connectors |
| Transport bus | NATS JetStream | Already deployed, exactly-once, replay, KV, sovereign |
| Long-term storage | ClickHouse | Already deployed, columnar, 10-year retention, fast geo queries |
| Visualization | TAK Server | Already deployed, CoT standard, multi-client, field-proven |
| AI reasoning | Legacy (Claude on NATS) | Already deployed, subscribes to bus, generates CoT products |
| ETL platform | NOT Airbyte/NiFi/Kafka Connect | Too heavy, batch-oriented, cloud-first, wrong bus |
| Frontend | NOT custom dashboards | TAK IS the UI — don't duplicate maps |
---
## Summary
**Before:** 5 platforms, 24 containers, $48/mo extra, 12 feeds on TAK, code-heavy, fragmented, no AI access.
**After:** 1 binary, YAML configs, $0 extra, 50+ feeds on TAK, operator-configurable, unified on one bus, AI-powered correlation.
**Redpanda Connect is the missing piece.** It's the universal adapter between "every data source in the world" and "our sovereign NATS bus." It was literally built for this pattern — and its native NATS JetStream support means zero translation layer between collection and our fabric.
---
*"The nervous system doesn't write code for every nerve ending. It just connects them."*
*That's what Redpanda Connect does for OneMind.*
